## What this is

By default the `+` button left of the composer opens a file picker. Everything else you may want to point the model at — a browser tab you are looking at, an earlier conversation, a skill, an MCP server, one of the plugins installed on this machine — has to be typed by hand, or referenced with `@`.

`dsh-composer-launcher` replaces that button with a **three-group menu**:

| Group | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Add** | files and folders, earlier chats, plan mode, goal mode |
| **Capabilities** | slash commands, skills, MCP servers |
| **Common plugins** | one row per installed plugin, plus an "all plugins" row |

What you pick does not get pasted in as text. It becomes a **reference chip** on a rail above the input box — the same native chip kind the host already renders for `@` references — and only turns into message text when you actually send.

There is also an **optional browser extension** (`DSH Tab Bridge`) which pushes your real browser's tabs to the plugin over a loopback HTTP bridge, so the Tabs row lists the pages you genuinely have open rather than a throwaway debug instance.

---

## What it does

### 1. The `+` menu (three groups)

A 360px panel, opened from the button at the `conversation.input.left` slot.

- **Add** — *Files and folders* (the host's own picker, multi-select, drag-and-drop; falls back to `@` references when the host exposes no folder picker), *Chats* (via `remote.sessionReferenceResolver`; chats only, no files), *Plan*, *Goal*.
- **Capabilities** — *Commands* (whatever the host's slash-command service offers), *Skills* (read live with `ctx.remote.skills.list({ sessionId })`), *MCP* (needs the host's `remote.mcpManager`).
- **Common plugins** — one row per plugin returned by `ctx.remote.pluginInventory.list()`. That list is read from the host on every load, so installing, removing or disabling a plugin is reflected immediately and there is no cache to keep in sync. Three modes decide which rows appear: `pinned`, `frequent`, `mixed` (see [Settings](#settings)).

Every row can be switched off individually from the settings card.

### 2. Reference chips

Picked items land on a rail **above** the input box (`conversation.input.dock`). A chip is `{ label, kind, icon }` plus an optional `url`, where `kind` is one of `web`, `plugin`, `skill`, `mcp`. Clicking the `×` removes it.

Two properties are worth naming, because both were bugs before they were features:

- **A web chip keeps its address.** A page title with no URL is useless to whoever reads the message — the chip carries the URL and the payload includes it.
- **A session reference stays a chip.** Writing a reference back through the plain-text draft API silently downgrades it to body text; the plugin renders it as a chip instead and never round-trips it through the text editor.

Chips are **per session**, so two chat tabs never share a rail.

On send, each chip is serialised into the message with a short marker, so the model can tell a referenced page from an attached file:

| Chip kind | Marker |
|---|---|
| web page | `【参考网页】<title> — <url>` |
| plugin | `【使用插件】<name>` |
| skill | `【技能】<name>` |
| MCP server | `【MCP】<name>` |

> These markers are literal and stay in Chinese in both interface languages. They are part of the text the **model** reads, not interface copy — translating them would change what the model sees.

### 3. Settings card

Registered on the `settings.plugin.item` slot as a card titled **Launcher** — 「启动器」 in the Chinese interface. It is collapsed the first time you open it and remembers that choice. All twelve fields are listed under [Settings](#settings).

### 4. Debug browser (fallback)

The Tabs row can also read tabs over a remote-debugging port from a Chromium process it starts itself. That is what **Launch debug browser** does — and when the extension is staged, the same call attaches it with `--load-extension` and then verifies through the debugging port that it really mounted, so this route needs no manual step at all (see [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)). It stays a fallback rather than the primary path because it only ever sees that one throwaway-profile instance, never the browser you already have open.

### 5. Loopback bridge

The host half owns a small HTTP bridge on `127.0.0.1:43130` (override: `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT`) so the extension can push tabs into it. It binds loopback only, yields politely if an older instance already holds the port, and is used for nothing else.

---

## Screenshots

**The `+` menu — Add / Capabilities / Common plugins — with the Tabs row fed by the extension**

![The composer + menu with the Tabs group and the connected extension](screenshots/01-composer-menu-tab-bridge.png)

**The Tabs row reading a real Microsoft Edge window over the bridge**

![Tab list pushed from Microsoft Edge](screenshots/02-tab-list-edge.png)

**The MCP servers the Capabilities group can reference — the row is built from the host's `remote.mcpManager`**

![MCP servers listed by the host](screenshots/03-mcp-servers.png)

**The plugin inventory the Common plugins group is built from, including its "N / M" narrowing counter**

![Plugin inventory with composition filtering](screenshots/04-plugin-inventory.png)

---

## The browser extension

The plugin works without it — the Tabs row simply says the extension is not installed and points at the button. With it, the row lists the tabs of your **everyday browser**.

### Three ways to get it loaded

Chromium will not let anything silently sideload an extension into the browser you use every day. That is a browser security rule with no plugin-side workaround, so the goal is a different one: make every *remaining* step either automatic or one click.

| Route | What happens | Manual steps |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a browser this plugin starts** | The plugin spawns a separate Chromium process with `--load-extension` pointing at the staged copy, then **verifies through the debugging port that the extension really mounted** | none |
| **B — your everyday browser** | The Tabs row offers *Open the extensions page* and *Copy the extension path*, so loading it once is a paste and a "Load unpacked" | one time, ~20 seconds |
| **C — managed machines** | Chromium enterprise policy (`ExtensionSettings` / `ExtensionInstallForcelist`) pointing at a self-hosted, signed CRX plus an HTTPS update manifest | admin rights; **not shipped here** |

**Route A is verified, not assumed.** After launching, the plugin asks the debugging port for its raw target list and looks for *this* extension's own worker (`chrome-extension://<id>/background.js`) rather than "some extensio

plugins.description: 给 DSH 里助手回复加气泡底，可选液态玻璃材质；工具条、过程行、统计行等周边信息也能一起同步
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-assistant-bubble [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) 使用皮肤插件从wallpaper里导入深色壁纸时，会发现ai回复的文字是无背景的，导致字和壁纸糊在一起无法阅读。所以让大肥鱼单独写了一个小插件实现气泡功能。 这下可以愉快地使用壁纸了。 . 有一些气泡间距的小问题，可能对观感有小影响，但是不太好修，所以就放在那里了， 插件开启前 开启后。气泡透明度之类的可以自己调，单独在设置里开了“助手回复气泡”的分区页。 ————以下内容都是肥鱼写的 给 DSH 里**助手回复**加一层自己的气泡底，可选液态玻璃材质；工具条、过程行、统计行等周边信息也能一起同步。 ## 为什么需要它 DSH 官方会话界面里，气泡（`..._bubble`）只属于**你发送的消息**；助手回复是一段**没有背景**的正文， 直接压在壁纸上。所以壁纸 / 皮肤类插件的"气泡不透明度""玻璃透明度"都管不到助手回复 —— 深色壁纸下助手的字就看不清了。这个插件补的就是这一块。 ## 功能 - **助手回复气泡**：圆角 + 可调底色；可选液态玻璃（白釉高光 + 模糊 + 厚玻璃折射 + 落地阴影）。 - **周边信息同步**：工具条（复制 / 点赞 / 分享 / 用量 / 时间）、过程折叠行、过程分组头（运行中）、 思考触发条、会话统计行、上下文占用环、运行行 —— 同一份材质、同一组参数，滑块一动一起变。 - **只给"真的有内容"的元素画底**：每个锚点都先核对有没有看得见的文字（≥2 个字）或可见的按钮 / 图标， 空壳一律不画 —— 所以不会出现"只有底色、没有文字"的空白气泡。 - **「工作步骤展示」明细行**：工具调用行（「运行命令」「网页获取」等）与「思考」行也有气泡 —— **折叠**时是紧凑小胶囊、**展开**时保持宿主原本的大横条。 - **操作条常驻**：取消宿主"非最后一条要悬停才显示"的门控。 - **宽度跟随内容**：气泡不拉满整行。 - **宽表格收进气泡**：宿主原本让宽表格按滚动容器整屏出血，这里改为气泡内横向滚动。 - **无障碍**：系统开启「减少透明度」时自动去掉模糊与白釉。 ## 安装 ```bash # 从 GitHub 安装（最新 main） dsh plugin --profile web add github:yutianliang/dsh-assistant-bubble ``` 官方桌面端也可以走侧边栏 **插件** 页 → 添加插件 → 填 `github:yutianliang/dsh-assistant-bubble`。 本地改代码时用 `link:`：`dsh plugin --profile web add link:E:\path\to\dsh-assistant-bubble`。 卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-assistant-bubble`。 ## 设置 安装后，**设置 →「助手回复气泡」**（独立分区，10 个控件）： | 控件 | 作用 | 默认 | | --- | --- | --- | | 液态玻璃 | 白釉高光 + 模糊 + 厚玻璃折射；关掉 = 平实心气泡 | 开 | | 周边信息同步 | 上面那七处周边信息是否同材质 | 开 | | 气泡不透明度 | 关闭液态玻璃时的底色浓度 | 60% | | 玻璃底色浓度 | 玻璃挡下的底色浓度，越高越不透 | 50% | | 雾化 | 玻璃的模糊半径 | 3px | | 玻璃颜色 | 6 个预设色块 + 取色器自定义 | #ffffff（深色 #12141a） | | 白釉强度 | 表面高光与边缘折射强度，0–200% | 100% | | 深色单独设置 | 打开后深色主题用另一套上面四项 | 关 | 值保存在浏览器本地 `localStorage["dsh-assistant-bubble:settings"]`（清缓存会回默认值）。 ## 兼容性 - **不声明 `engines` / `peerDependencies`**：安装与启用不会被版本检查拦下。 - 客户端半区**不声明** `dsh.client.inject`：模块无条件加载，气泡样式一定生效； `slots` / `locale` 两个服务用 `ctx.inject` 运行时等待，拿不到只丢设置页。 - 唯一外部依赖是宿主写在 DOM 上的语义属性与 CSS-Module 类名后缀。宿主大版本更新后最坏的情况是 **样式静默失效**（看起来像没装），不会报错、不会牵连其它插件。 ## 实现要点 所有参数走 CSS 变量，设置页把值内联写到 `body` 上： ``` --dab-solid-alpha 实心气泡底浓度 --dab-glass-alpha 玻璃挡底浓度 --dab-glass-color 玻璃色（r, g, b） --dab-blur 雾化半径 --dab-sheen 白釉强度倍数 ``` 玻璃配方对齐 [`dsh-plugin-wallpaper-engine`](https://github.com/elysia395/dsh-wallpaper-engine) 的玻璃面： 白釉渐变 + `blur() saturate(1.3) brightness(1.04)` + 双向内阴影折射 + 落地阴影。 ### 思考面板的标题行 展开「思考」时，宿主会给面板内部的**粘性标题行**铺一层实心底色（`--dsw-alias-bg-base`，深色主题下近黑， 展开后就是压在内容上的一条黑带）。这里把它换成**同一颜色的半透明版**并保留吸顶： ```css background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dsw-alias-bg-base) 80%, transparent) ``` 滚到顶部时仍能遮住下方内容，但不再是一条实心黑条。（不用 `backdrop-filter`：那会把下方的浅色文字 糊成一条白带。） ### 挂在哪些锚点上 | 位置 | 锚点 | | --- | --- | | 助手回复正文 | `[data-chat-flow-kind="assistant-step"] div[class*="_root"] > div[class*="_body"]` | | 工具条（复制 / 点赞 / 用量 / 时间） | `[data-turn-tail] [class*="_actions"]` | | 过程折叠行「已完成，用时 N 秒」 | `[data-turn-process]` | | 过程分组头「正在分析请求 · ⋯」 | `[data-process-activity]` | | 思考触发条 | `[data-turn-trigger]` | | 工具调用行（运行命令 / 网页获取…） | `[data-tool] [data-disclosure-row]` | | 「思考」行 | `[data-variant="think"] [data-disclosure-row]` | | 会话统计行「N 轮 M 步 · tok/s」 | `[data-composer-stats]` | | 上下文占用环「41%」 | `button[class*="_trigger"]:has(> svg[viewBox="0 0 14 14"])` | | 运行行「深度求索中⋯」 | `[data-chat-running]` | | 宽表格 | `.md-table-wide` | ## 开发 实现细节、设计取舍与踩过的坑见 [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)。 ## License MIT

plugins.description: DSH 原生抖音助手：有限自主观看、共享人格与兴趣记忆、原生设置和观看日报。
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH 抖音助手

让 DSH 里的 DeepSeek（大肥鱼）自己刷抖音：搜索、换片、看真实画面，把有意思的内容记下来，并在你许可的范围内分享给好友。

在专用 Edge 里浏览电脑网页版抖音，每隔几秒采样视频画面交给模型。所有外发功能默认关闭，每一项都有独立开关、次数上限和时间限制。这是第三方适配，不是 DeepSeek 官方出品。

## 能做什么

| 功能 | 说明 | 默认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 自主观看 | 按人格和兴趣自己搜索、换片、继续看或停止，并给出理由 | 需手动开始有限轮次 |
| 兴趣与人格 | 兴趣来自实际观看进度和已确认行为，不是看到主题就算喜欢 | 随观看自动积累 |
| 时间限制 | 每日允许时段（北京时间）加单轮时长，到点视频真的暂停 | 单轮 10 分钟 |
| 静默观看 | 静音，核对窗口归属后尝试最小化（仍是有窗口的 Edge，不是 headless） | 关闭 |
| 观看日报 | 把当天实际看过的标题、作者、链接汇总成 Markdown，不调用模型 | 可手动生成，每轮观看结束后也会尝试生成 |
| 主动分享 | 通过官方分享界面把当前看过的作品发给许可好友，每天默认 3 次 | 关闭 |
| 自动问候 | 每位许可好友每天最多一次，合计默认 2 次，带「自动问候」标记 | 关闭 |
| 私信自动回复 | 只处理你确认的最多两位好友，只回复启动之后的新消息 | 关闭 |
| 公开评论 | 每天默认 3 条，每轮 1 条，同一作品只评论一次 | 关闭 |
| 音频理解 | 本地 Whisper 转写对白，可选 MiMo 或 MiniMax 云端 | 关闭 |

发送结果不确定时一律暂停，不会自动重发。

## 两种用法

| | 插件版 | 软件版 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 在哪用 | DSH 的「设置 → 刷抖音」，全部用按钮操作 | 独立的 Windows 桌面软件，对话式下任务 |
| 模型 | 用 DSH 里已配置的提供商 | 用你自己填的 DeepSeek API Key |
| 版本 | 1.3 | 已打包的是 1.2.0，1.3 尚未打包 |

两者共用同一份人格、兴趣和记忆，但同一时刻只会运行一个自主观看。

## 快速开始（插件版）

需要 Windows、Microsoft Edge、Node.js 22.13 以上，以及 DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 系列（已在 DSH Desktop 2.0.17 上核对过设置页）。

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/LockyBee/dsh-douyin-agent.git
cd dsh-douyin-agent
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
$dshInstallDirectory = 'C:\Apps\DSH Desktop' # 替换为正在使用的 DSH 安装目录
.\install-native.ps1 -DshRoot $dshInstallDirectory
```

第一条命令安装依赖；不带 `-Install` 的脚本只做检查，不改配置也不开窗口。确认无误后完全退出 DSH，再执行：

```powershell
.\install-native.ps1 -DshRoot $dshInstallDirectory -Install
```

重新打开 DSH，在「设置」里找到「刷抖音」，按这个顺序用：

1. 基础设置：选提供商和模型（模型必须支持图片），保存。
2. 视频观看：点「打开抖音」，在专用 Edge 里自己登录或过验证。
3. 设置允许时段和单轮时长，点「开始有限轮次」，再点「开始自主观看」。

安装细节和本机现有入口的说明见 [插件说明](docs/plugin.md)。

## 当前验证状态

| 状态 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 真实环境验证过 | 推荐播放、搜索、上下切换、暂停、画面采样、限时到点暂停；旧版 DSH 原生工具调用；表情图片采样；一次人工授权的好友转发；DSH 2.0.17 中设置页挂载并读回状态 |
| 只有合成测试 | 自主分享、行为偏好、自动问候、自主评论、静默、日报 |
| 还没验证 | 抖音最小化后的持续播放、真实评论区、收到新私信后的完整自动回复、MiMo 与 MiniMax 云端、标准 bundle 安装 |

合成测试用的是替身模型和临时页面，不能当作真实抖音上能用的证据。最新测试数字和已知失败见 [v10 验证记录](docs/verification/native-v10.md)。

## 目录

| 位置 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-plugin.mjs`、`client.js`、`cordis.bundle.yml` | 原生插件入口、设置页前端、标准 bundle 声明 |
| `tool-definitions.mjs` | 32 项工具目录，插件和软件共用 |
| `native-*.mjs` | 设置页后端、模型路由、人格注入、问候与观看决策 |
| `core.mjs`、`browser-*.mjs` | 专用 Edge 的控制、采样、限时 |
| `video-limits.mjs`、`task-limits.mjs`、`watch-mode.mjs` | 时段与轮次、任务预算、静默 |
| `autonomous-*.mjs`、`spark-*.mjs`、`daily-report.mjs` | 自主观看、分享、评论、问候、日报 |
| `chat-*.mjs`、`message-tracker.mjs`、`outbound-send.mjs` | 私信自动回复和统一的发送账本 |
| `memory.mjs`、`persona-memory.mjs`、`qq-sync.mjs` | 共享记忆、人格卡、QQ 侧同步 |
| `app.mjs`、`api-agent.mjs`、`public/`、`start-api.*` | 旧的本机 HTTP 控制台（`http://127.0.0.1:3218`） |
| `desktop/` | Electron 桌面软件的源码、打包脚本和上游许可证 |
| `media/` | 可选音频模块，内置三份社区项目源码 |
| `tests/`、`verification/` | 单元测试，以及实机验收脚本 |
| `skill/SKILL.md` | 给模型看的使用说明 |

## 文档

| 文档 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| [插件说明](docs/plugin.md) | 插件安装、设置页逐项说明、预算、各项外发的规则 |
| [独立软件说明](docs/standalone-api.md) | 独立 API 控制台和软件版的配置 |
| [详细说明](docs/details.md) | 原 README 全文，按时间累积，内容多 |
| [功能复用与来源](docs/reuse.md) | 参考和复用的开源项目，以及边界 |
| [docs/verification/](docs/verification) | 各版本的测试记录 |
| [desktop/README.md](desktop/README.md) | 桌面软件的构建和使用 |
| [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) | 第三方许可证 |

## 开发

```powershell
pnpm test
pnpm run test:native
```

`pnpm test` 会起临时 Edge 页面，不碰真实抖音和你的账号。运行状态、浏览器资料、密钥、数据库、私信正文和联系人信息都只保存在本机，不进入仓库。

## 许可证

本项目原创代码采用 [MIT](LICENSE)。第三方源码和依赖的原许可证、版权及通知见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

公开准备、分发包检查与社区市场申请见 [发布记录](docs/publication.md)。

plugins.description: Hermes in the DSH sidebar: gateway + dashboard control, Hermes own health report, and the DSH <-> Hermes bridge. Generated mirror of plugins/hermes-panel - do not edit here.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-hermes-panel

[中文文档](README.zh.md) | English

> **`1.1.0-rc.1` — a pre-release, published on purpose before it is finished.** It is on npm and in the
> market so that it can be installed, used and broken by someone other than its author, which is the only
> test that was ever going to catch the interesting bugs. Install it the same way as anything else; the
> version number is the honest part.

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sidebar panel for the
**native [Hermes](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) agent**: it finds your Hermes
installation, starts and stops its messaging gateway and web dashboard, and embeds the native
dashboard in a panel.

There is **no Hermes panel in the left sidebar**. The plugin registers nothing there.
It ships **one seat**: a `Hermes` tab in the right column, opened from the ⊕ list's
**Open Hermes** row, with three faces switched by a row of icons in its strip (the
active one is marked, each has a tooltip):

| | |
|---|---|
| 🌐 | **Dashboard** — an iframe of the native Hermes dashboard, beside the conversation rather than in place of it: DSH on the left, Hermes on the right, one window |
| 💬 | **Record** — the Hermes ↔ DSH exchange, read from DSH's own session logs; every row says which directory it ran in |
| ⚙ | **Setup** — the health report and upgrade, the DSH bridge, and the shared workspace |

The same strip carries **start / stop**, **restart**, and **↗ open in a new tab**.

The tab belongs to no session, so it rides the conversation view: switching sessions
keeps it, and switching faces never reloads the page — the iframe never leaves the
document, it is only hidden.
| Health † | runs Hermes' own `official-web/doctor.ps1 -Json` and renders its nine-point report |
| Upgrade † | runs `check-update.ps1` to report, then `update.ps1 -Apply` to upgrade — stopping Hermes first, and **not** starting it again |
| Directories | the two settings the whole plugin reads — the runtime (Hermes' `VENV`) and the data directory (`HERMES_HOME`) — each with a folder picker and the evidence that the folder is the right one |
| DSH bridge | both halves of the DSH ↔ Hermes channel: writes `mcp_servers.dsh` into Hermes' `config.yaml`, diagnoses the MCP client version each profile resolves, and hands Hermes a **session id** so it can review a result and send a follow-up into the same session |
| Shared workspace | one directory both agents work in; the `AGENTS.md` inside it is read by both, so shared context needs no conversion |
| Configuration | two directories — a runtime and a volume. Nothing is guessed: an empty setting means a default under the DSH home, and the panel prints what it found there |
| Languages | Chinese and English, chosen at runtime |
| Platform | Windows (process control uses `netstat` / `taskkill`; see [Platform](#platform)) |

† **These two are the `official-web` distribution's own maintenance scripts.** An upstream
Hermes — `pip install hermes-agent`, data in a home directory with `config.yaml` — has none of
them, and there is no `hermes-agent` equivalent to call instead, so the panel **disables both
and says why** rather than offering a button that fails. Everything else (start/stop, the
dashboard, the record, the bridge, the shared workspace) works on any installation, and
`GET /hermes/api/status` reports the set as `capabilities`.

> **Not to be confused with `hermes-web-ui`.** That npm package brands itself *Ekko Studio* and
> used to be named *Hermes Studio*. This plugin targets the **native** Hermes Python agent
> (`hermes_agent`, `HERMES_HOME`), not that one.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @guanyang14700/dsh-hermes-panel
```

Restart `dsh` afterwards — the **host** half is a Node module and browser refreshes do not reload it.
The panel then appears in the sidebar as **Hermes**.

### What it needs

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `>= 0.2.0-rc.2 < 1.0.0` (a peer dependency, checked by the panel and reported per profile) |
| Hermes | any installation the plugin can recognise — upstream (`pip`/`pipx`/`uv`, home with `config.yaml`), or the `official-web` distribution (home with `official-web/.env`). **Hermes is not bundled and not installed by this plugin**; the panel is told where it is |
| Optional | `official-web/` inside that home — its four PowerShell scripts are what 体检 / 查更新 / 升级 / 安装 wrap. Without it those three controls are disabled |
| For the DSH bridge | a `python` (the one carrying `hermes-agent`), a `node`, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `~/.dsh/.env` |
| OS | Windows. Process control shells out to `netstat` / `taskkill`, and the maintenance scripts are PowerShell — see [Platform](#platform) |

> Development checkouts use `@guanyang14700/dsh-hermes-panel` through a `link:` dependency. See
> [PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md) for the rename procedure and what has to follow it — the profile
> needs the package linked under its new name before DSH can resolve the bundle.

## Runtime and volume

Nothing about *this machine* is hard-coded, and nothing is guessed. Two directories are named:

- **Runtime** — the Python environment Hermes runs in (its `VENV`). Empty means
  `<DSH home>/hermes-panel/runtime`.
- **Data directory** — `HERMES_HOME`: profiles, sessions, state, `config.yaml`, `official-web/`.
  Empty means `<DSH home>/hermes-panel/home`.

They are independent, on purpose: point the data directory at an existing Hermes to keep using its
sessions and keys, and point the runtime at whatever Python should run it. A machine with neither
gets both under the DSH home.

The only directory guessed at all is `HERMES_HOME` from the environment, and that is Hermes' own
variable, honoured after the settings.

**Earlier versions walked the filesystem looking for a sibling `Hermes` — a chain of ancestors,
the user profile, a few dotted spellings — and that walk was the bug.** An installed plugin lives
several levels down inside a profile's `node_modules`, so the walk was always one directory short:
it reported no installation beside a Hermes that was running, and the panel lost its start button.
Two named directories replaced it, and every failure now names the directory it looked at.

The CLI is resolved in this order: the runtime directory, `HERMES_EXE` from `official-web/.env`,
then **`hermes` on PATH**. A home with no runnable CLI is still reported as found — the panel shows
its status, its settings and the bridge, and says which setting to fill before it can start
anything.

If nothing is found, the panel says so and lists every path it tried. **Re-detect** re-runs the
search, so installing Hermes while the panel is open is picked up without restarting DSH.

### Settings

Because empty values mean *detect this*, override only what you need.

**Where to change them:** open the **Plugins** panel in the sidebar (the entry that installs and
manages plugins) and, under the **Official** group, click the **Hermes Panel settings** card. That
card exists because this plugin registers its own settings page into the panel's `plugins.item`
slot — see [why that is necessary](#why-the-settings-page-registers-itself).

> The panel lists this plugin **twice**, and both entries are real. Under **Installed** is the
> bundle card with the enable/disable switch; under **Official** is the settings page. They are
> named differently on purpose: two identically titled cards, only one of which carries the form,
> is how you end up opening the wrong one.

The same values live in the profile's own patch layer, which is what a settings save writes:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `runtimeDir` | `''` | Python environment (Hermes' `VENV`); empty = `<DSH home>/hermes-panel/runtime` |
| `dataDir` | `''` | `HERMES_HOME`; empty = `<DSH home>/hermes-panel/home` |
| `dashboardPort` | `0` | `0` = `DASHBOARD_PORT` from `.env`, else 9150 |
| `sharedWorkspace` | `''` | a directory both agents work in; empty = no sharing |
| `manageGateway` | `true` | start/stop the messaging gateway along with the dashboard |
| `autostart` | `false` | bring Hermes up when the plugin activates |

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-create-dialog

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Create Workspace** dialog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a name and go, or pick a folder with a chooser that finally remembers where you were.

![The Create Workspace dialog: a name field, a workspace folder row with a Choose folder button, and a New workspace location row with a Change button](docs/create-workspace.png)

## What it does

Clicking **Add workspace…** in DSH today opens the OS folder dialog immediately. This plugin replaces that with a small dialog that asks two independent questions: what is the workspace called, and where does it live. Answer the first only and it creates the folder for you; answer the second and the folder you picked *is* the workspace.

| You do | You get |
| --- | --- |
| Type a name, press **Create** | A new folder with that name is created under **New workspace location**, registered as a workspace, and a session opens in it |
| Click **Choose folder…** | The native Windows folder dialog, starting **where you left off**, not at some default |
| Choose a folder, leave the name empty | The name fills itself in from the folder's own name |
| Choose a folder, having typed a name | Your name wins — the workspace is registered, then renamed to it |
| Click **Change…** on New workspace location | Pick where name-only workspaces go from now on; the choice is saved and survives restarts |
| Cancel / Esc / click the backdrop | Nothing happens — no folder, no registration |

### The effect, before and after

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating `my-project` | Create the folder in Explorer first, then hunt for it in the picker | Type `my-project`. Done |
| The folder picker's starting point | The OS default, every single time | The directory you last chose |
| Where new workspaces land | Wherever you navigate to | A location you set once, visible in the dialog, changeable any time |
| Naming a workspace after its folder | Retype the folder name | Auto-filled |

## Install

### From the DSH UI (simplest)

Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, paste this address, click **Install**, then **Enable now**:

```text
https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
```

That box takes a package name, a Git address, a tarball or a local absolute path. A repository URL works because this package ships a `dsh.bundle` patch — DSH checks exactly that before it installs. Restart DeepSeek Harness if the plugin does not come up.

Two things worth knowing: it downloads straight from GitHub, so GitHub has to be reachable (the China-mirror option only covers registry packages, not repository downloads); and DSH does not auto-update third-party plugins yet — upgrading means uninstall + install again.

> Already installed with `tools/install.mjs` below? Run `node tools/install.mjs --uninstall` first, so the profile does not end up with two loader rows for the same id.

### One-line prompt for your agent

If you would rather not click through it:

```text
Install the DSH plugin at https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog into my DSH and tell me when to restart.
```

### From the plugin market (once listed)

Search for **dsh-workspace-create-dialog** in [dshmarket](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) and install it in one click. The listing is [pending a PR](contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/) to [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) (their CI requires the repository to be at least one day old); until it lands, use the routes above and below.

### Manual install from this repository

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
cd dsh-workspace-create-dialog
node tools/install.mjs
```

That copies the package into your DSH profile's `node_modules` and appends one loader line to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. It resolves your DSH home the same way the harness does — explicit config, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh`.

**Then restart DeepSeek Harness** (the host half is a Node module, so a config reload alone will not import it). After that, changing `lib/client.js` only needs a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` still needs a restart.

`node tools/install.mjs --dry-run` prints what it would do without writing anything; `--uninstall` removes the package and its loader row again.

Publishing to npm is **not** required: the market installs from GitHub exactly the same way, and listing is unaffected either way.

## How it works

### It uses the official extension point, not a patch

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` declares a `single` slot where the "pick a directory" step is handed to whichever plugin fills it:

```text
sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow              ← the sidebar's "Add workspace…"
conversation.hero.workspace.directoryFlow     ← the empty-state entry
```

The owner hands the occupant the whole interaction contract:

```ts
interface DirectoryFlowOwnerProps {
  open: boolean                     // a pick is requested
  busy: boolean                     // the owner is adopting the picked path
  onPicked: (path: string) => void  // report the directory; the owner registers it and opens a session
  onCancel: () => void
  onError: (message: string) => void
}
```

This plugin registers its own occupant into both slots at **priority -100**. A `single` slot renders the lowest-priority entry, the shipped native driver sits at `0`, so this dialog wins (two entries at the *same* priority throw, which is the official protection against ambiguity). Removing the loader line from your profile patch restores the stock behaviour exactly.

### Why the folder dialog is built here instead of reused

The desktop app opens its folder dialog from the Electron main process without a starting directory:

```js
// D:\App\DSH\resources\app.asar → lib/main.js
dialog.showOpenDialog(window, { properties: ['openDirectory', 'createDirectory'] })
```

There is no `defaultPath`, which is exactly why the chooser always starts in the same place. A plugin cannot reach that call: the DSH host is a *child process* of Electron. So `lib/pick-folder.js` opens its own `IFileDialog` — a small C# COM interop compiled and run by the **Windows PowerShell 5.1 that ships with Windows**:

- **no dependencies**: no koffi, no PowerShell 7, no native module to publish;
- compilation happens **in memory** (~120 ms per call), so there is no DLL cache to corrupt or lock;
- the one line that matters is `IFileDialog::SetFolder` — the remembered directory as the starting point;
- the dialog runs in a child process, so a native fault cannot take the host down.

The C# method declaration order must match the COM vtable (`Show=3`, `SetOptions=9`, `SetFolder=12`, `SetTitle=17`, `GetResult=20`). Getting it wrong does not error — it just silently does the wrong thing — so a self-test asserts the order.

## Where name-only workspaces are created

The **New workspace location** is resolved in this order (`lib/base-dir.js`, a pure function):

1. **What you set in the dialog** — highest priority; once you change it, it is yours;
2. **`config.baseDir`** from your profile patch — the value used at install time;
3. **The root of your default workspace** — the parent of the workspace whose directory is named `default-workspace` (a name the harness fixes, independent of UI language). New workspaces land next to it. This is the default for a fresh install;
4. **Fallback** — `<Documents>/deepseek-harness`, or `<home>/deepseek-harness` when there is no Documents folder.

The resolved value is written to the state file, so "what it was on first run" is decided once and only you change it afterwards. `config.baseDir` is a seed, not an order.

## HTTP routes

All four are loopback-guarded (loopback socket + loopback `Host` + same-origin marker; `x-forwarded-for` is never trusted) — they create directories and open windows on the host machine, so nothing off-machine may reach them.

| Route | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/config` | GET | Current location + last directory |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/base-dir` | POST | `{"

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-better-wechat

> 把电脑上的微信聊天，变成你随时能问的私人消息工作台。
> **本地优先：采集、解密、索引、筛选都在你的电脑上完成；只有你这次分析真正用到的消息文本，才会交给你在 DSH 里选择的模型。**

微信里其实躺着大量有价值的信息 —— 谁答应了什么、哪条通知有时限、上周讨论的结论是什么。但真要用的时候，你只能在几百个会话里往上翻。

`dsh-better-wechat` 是 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)（DSH）的一个插件。它在你的电脑本地把微信聊天整理成一份**可检索、可筛选、可追溯**的私人档案，然后让 DSH 里的助手用自然语言帮你查、帮你总结、帮你把「要做的事」挑出来。

- 🗂️ **一句话找消息** —— 按人、按群、按时间、按关键词找，返回原文和上下文
- ✅ **自动整理待办** —— 从聊天里挑出与你有关的承诺和截止时间，每条都带原文出处
- 🔕 **免打扰群一键忽略** —— 整理消息时跳过你早已静音的群，只看真正重要的会话
- 🔒 **本地优先、按需外发** —— 数据库、索引和完整历史留在本机；只有本次分析用到的消息文本交给 DSH 里的模型，换成本地模型即可完全不外发

---

## 它把什么变简单了

| 你现在的麻烦 | 用它可以这样 |
| --- | --- |
| 重要信息淹没在几百个群聊里 | 直接问「昨天关于验收的消息」，拿到原文和上下文 |
| 每天翻聊天记录找「谁答应了什么」 | 让它按日期整理候选待办，逐条附上消息依据 |
| 几十个免打扰群刷屏，整理时全是噪声 | 说一句「忽略免打扰群」，整理范围立刻干净 |
| 想知道「这事上周谁提的」 | 按时间回看，结论可追溯到具体某条消息 |
| 不想把聊天记录交给云端工具 | 采集、索引、完整历史都在本机；只把你选中的文本交给模型分析，也可以改用本地模型完全不外发 |

---

## 核心功能

### 1. 用大白话检索聊天记录
不需要记命令，也不需要知道消息存在哪个数据库。直接描述你记得的线索：谁、哪个群、大概什么时候、聊了什么。

> 「上周三到周五，项目群里提到的截止时间」
> 「查一下昨天跟王工讨论的接口问题，给我原文」

### 2. 把聊天里的「事」挑出来
它会通读你指定时间范围内的消息，整理成候选待办：任务、负责人、截止时间、状态，并且每条都标注来自哪条消息。

更重要的是它的分寸感：
- **草稿不等于完成** —— 它给你的都是需要你核对的草稿，不会替你确认「已完成」
- **别人的事不算你的事** —— 群里的任务不会硬算到你头上
- **证据可回溯** —— 消息更新后会标记「依据已变化」，可以按版本回查当时的原文

> 「整理本周与我有关的待办，明确任务和可能任务分开」

### 3. 免打扰群，一键忽略
这是最好用的一条「减负开关」。

你手机里静音的群，插件读的是**微信自己的「消息免打扰」设置**，所以和你在微信里看到的是一回事。整理消息时开启忽略，免打扰群的海量消息就不会占用你的整理时间和模型上下文。

- 只排除**确定**处于免打扰的会话；状态不明的会话会保留，不会被误伤
- 会明确告诉你索引里是否已有免打扰信息，缺数据时不会假装「已排除」

> 「整理今天的待办，忽略免打扰群」

### 4. 会话视角：先找准人，再查内容
同名群、同名联系人很容易搞混。插件会先列出匹配到的会话（真实显示名、类型、消息量、最近时间、是否免打扰），确认后再读取内容 —— 不会擅自替你选一个。

### 5. 长期不关注名单
有些群你永远不想在整理时看到。可以把它们加入「长期不关注」名单：之后所有检索、上下文和待办都会自动跳过，但它仍然保留在本地档案里，随时可以查看或移出。

### 6. 结论带证据，越权的事不做
每条结论都能落到具体某条消息。插件不会发消息、不会改微信、不会替你执行任务、不会创建提醒 —— 它只做「读懂 + 整理」。

---

## 三分钟上手

**第 0 步 · 准备**：DSH（支持 workspace bundle 的版本）、Python 3.10+。要让插件自动读取电脑微信，还需要 Windows 上的微信 4.x 并已登录。

**第 1 步 · 安装插件**
在 DSH 的插件页面安装本插件目录（或让 `plugin_manager` 用 `install_bundle` 安装）。
> ⚠️ 首次安装本地插件目录后，请**完整退出并重新打开 DSH**。仅刷新或禁用/启用不能替代重启 —— 插件代码必须由宿主重新加载，新的工具才会出现。

**第 2 步 · 让它读一次微信**
安装完成后，在 DSH 里说：

> 「初始化微信助手」

插件会接入你已登录的电脑微信，做一次完整读取、校验并建立本地索引（首次通常需要几分钟）。若提示缺少采集依赖，运行插件目录里的 `安装采集依赖.cmd` 后重试。

**第 3 步 · 开始提问**
> 「看看今天有哪些需要我回的消息」

之后每天想更新时，说一句「刷新微信记录」即可，不需要重新选择来源。

> 没有 Windows 微信也没关系：可以导入已有的聊天导出（完整导出目录即可），macOS / Linux 同样支持。

---

## 可以这样问它

- 「昨天群聊里关于验收的消息，给我原文和上下文」
- 「总结今天和这位联系人的讨论，每条结论给出消息依据」
- 「整理本周与我有关的待办，明确任务和可能任务分开，不把别人要做的事算到我名下」
- 「只提取今天上午 9 点到 12 点，项目甲群和项目乙群的记录」
- 「总结昨天的消息，排除闲聊群，不读公众号」
- 「以后不关注这个闲聊群 —— 先把匹配到的会话列出来给我确认」
- 「整理今天的待办，忽略免打扰群」

---

## 隐私：本地优先，但要看你把模型放在哪

先把话说清楚：**采集、解密、校验、索引、筛选、会话查找全部在你的电脑上完成，微信数据库、解密副本和完整索引不会上传到任何地方。**但插件不是“本地总结器”——分析必须由 DSH 里的模型来做，所以你要知道哪些内容会随模型请求离开本机。

| 留在本机 | 会交给 DSH 里的模型 |
| --- | --- |
| 微信数据库与其解密副本 | 本次分析**被选中的消息正文** |
| 完整聊天历史与全文索引 | 联系人 / 群显示名、时间、证据编号 |
| 账号映射、本地随机密钥 | 你提问里的时间 / 会话 / 类型范围 |
| 长期不关注名单、候选待办草稿 | — |

- **这不是“完全离线总结”。** 如果 DSH 用的是云端模型（例如 DeepSeek API），上表右列的内容会随模型请求发送给对应服务商。这不是插件在“上传”，而是“让模型帮你分析”本身的含义。
- **想让内容完全不外发**：在 DSH 里改用本地模型，那就真的不出本机。
- **你能控制发多少**：范围与条数由你决定——按日期、按会话、按类型筛选，用「忽略免打扰群」跳过高噪声会话，一次只读你真正要用的那几条。图片、语音、视频和文件正文不会被读取，未读取的内容会明确标注。
- **插件自己不碰微信**：不向微信写入数据、不注入进程、不保存数据库密钥、不发送消息、不执行任务、不创建提醒。

**插件主动发起的联网行为只有一个**：运行 `安装采集依赖.cmd` 时从公开源安装 Python 依赖包（与聊天内容无关）。其余网络流量来自 DSH 与它所选择的模型，遵循 DSH 自身的配置与权限。

> 完整的数据边界见 [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)，安全反馈见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

---

## 适用环境与边界（如实说明）

| 项目 | 情况 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH 宿主 | 已在 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` 真实运行时验证插件加载、工具注册、返回格式与审批 |
| 自动读取电脑微信 | 需要 Windows + 微信 4.x + Python 3.10+（64 位） |
| macOS / Linux | 支持导入已有聊天导出；不支持自动读取本机微信 |
| 图片 / 语音 / 视频 / 文件 | 只记录「有一条这样的消息」，不读取正文 |
| 实时性 | 读的是**本地快照**，不是实时聊天；空结果不等于「没有消息」，需要时先刷新 |
| 待办准确性 | 结论是需要人工核对的草稿；请以原文为准 |

---

## 常见问题

**会把我的聊天记录上传吗？**
分两层看。微信数据库、解密副本、完整索引和历史都只在本机，插件不会上传它们；但**被选中用于分析的那段文本会交给 DSH 里的模型**——如果那是云端模型，文本就会随模型请求发送给该服务商。想让内容完全不出本机，请把 DSH 换成本地模型。

**免打扰状态是怎么判断的？**
读的是微信自己的「消息免打扰」设置。状态不明的会话不会被当成「没开免打扰」，也不会被误排除。

**升级或改名后我的索引会丢吗？**
不会。私有数据目录与插件名字解耦：如果本机已有旧目录里的索引，改名后会继续使用它，不需要重新采集（也可以用环境变量 `DSH_WECHAT_STATE_DIR` 指定目录）。

**为什么重启 DSH 之后工具还是没出现？**
说明宿主没有重新加载插件。请在任务结束后正常重启 DSH；仅刷新页面或禁用/启用插件可能清不掉旧模块缓存。

**为什么有的时候查不到消息？**
常见原因是本地快照还没覆盖到那个时间段。状态信息会告诉你是否需要刷新，以及当前覆盖范围 —— 空结果不等于当天没有消息。

**支持多个微信账号吗？**
一个私有数据目录绑定一个账号。切换账号请使用另一个数据目录，避免混在一起。

---

## 深入一点

- 架构与数据边界：[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- 安装升级与排障：[docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)
- 发布流程：[docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md)
- 隐私说明：[PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) ｜ 安全反馈：[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) ｜ 参与贡献：[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ｜ 更新记录：[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

本项目原创部分采用 MIT，采集器上游改写部分采用 Apache-2.0，见 [第三方归属](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

---

<details>
<summary>附录 · 插件由哪些能力组成（排障与进阶使用）</summary>

插件按功能域拆成 5 个可独立启停的组件，每个组件只提供自己那组能力：

| 组件 | 能力 |
| --- | --- |
| `core` | 配置、本地引擎与审批状态（不直接提供工具） |
| `stage-one` | 读取与刷新本机聊天（`wechat_prepare`、`wechat_refresh`） |
| `read` | 状态、检索、上下文、按范围复核、会话查找（`wechat_status`、`wechat_search`、`wechat_context`、`wechat_review`、`wechat_conversations`） |
| `tasks` | 候选待办的保存与读取（`wechat_save_tasks`、`wechat_list_tasks`） |
| `preferences` | 长期不关注名单的查看与修改（`wechat_get_preferences`、`wechat_set_preferences`） |

常用范围参数：`start_date` / `end_date`、`start_time` / `end_time`、`kinds`（friend / group / official / private / system）、`conversation_ids`、`exclude_conversation_ids`、`exclude_muted`。
第一步只接受空参数；筛选与忽略全部发生在第二步。

</details>

# DSH 提示词增强器

**简体中文** ｜ [English](README.en.md)

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件。在输入框写提示词，点一下按钮，模型改写后替换输入框内容。

- 包名：`@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer`
- 仓库：https://github.com/JianYiAG/dsh-prompt-enhancer
- 许可：MIT

---

## 安装

**桌面端**：

1. 左侧栏进「插件」页
2. 安装 bundle，填 `@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer`
3. 完全退出应用后重新打开

**CLI / Web 端**：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer
```

CLI 安装后若未生效，在「插件」页勾选该插件，或把包名加入 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，然后重启应用。

安装与常见问题见 [DISTRIBUTION.md](DISTRIBUTION.md)。

---

## 使用

1. 在输入框输入提示词
2. 点模型选择器左侧的按钮
3. 按钮停止转动后，输入框内容已替换为改写结果；不满意可在输入框内撤销

输入框为空时按钮不显示。

也可输入 `/prompt-enhance 提示词`，结果以命令结果行显示，不写回输入框。

---

## 配置

默认使用当前会话的模型。可在 profile 补丁中指定固定模型：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: prompt-enhancer
      name: '@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer'
      config:
        provider: <provider-id>
        model: <model-id>
```

两个字段需同时提供；删除 `config` 即恢复使用会话模型。

---

## 卸载

桌面端在「插件」页卸载；CLI：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer
```

---

MIT

plugins.description: Per-workspace persistent memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): sidebar panel, automatic system-prompt injection, and an agent tool to save memories
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-memories

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-dsh-4D6BFE?style=flat-square&logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-workspace-memories?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-memories)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Per-workspace persistent memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH)** — a plugin that gives every workspace its own durable memory files, injects them into every session running in that workspace, and lets both you and the agent manage them.

## Why this plugin exists

DSH agents are stateless across sessions: everything a session "learns" — your project's decisions, conventions, hard-won debugging facts — lives only in that conversation's context and is gone when it ends. The built-in mechanism for durable knowledge is `AGENTS.md`, but it is a static, project-owned instruction file: the agent cannot update it on its own, and **some things should not live in the project folder at all** — server addresses and topologies, local environment quirks, machine-specific paths, personal working conventions. Anything under the project tree risks being committed to git by accident.

This plugin closes that gap with a small, explicit memory loop whose default storage is **outside the project directory**:

1. **Every workspace gets a memory directory** — by default under the DSH data directory (`~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace>/`), never inside the repo. Plain Markdown you can read, diff, and back up. (An opt-in `workspace` storage mode keeps memories in `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` for teams who *want* them versioned alongside the code.)
2. **Memories are injected automatically** — each session created in a workspace carries that workspace's memory files in its system prompt, alongside `AGENTS.md`, so a fresh session starts already "remembering".
3. **The agent can write memories itself** — a global `save_workspace_memory` tool lets any session persist a decision, server detail, convention, or preference the moment you say "remember this".
4. **You stay in control** — a sidebar panel lists, creates, edits, and deletes memory files per workspace, so memory stays inspectable and correctable instead of hidden in a database.

## Features

| Capability | Where |
|---|---|
| Browse / create / edit / delete memory files | **Workspace Memory** sidebar panel (switch workspaces via the selector) |
| Ask the agent to remember something | Any session: "remember: …" → the agent calls `save_workspace_memory` |
| Automatic recall | Every session in the workspace gets its memory files injected into its system prompt |

Works in every built-in agent preset (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator): the tool is registered in the root composition, and global tools are visible to all presets unless a custom preset opts out with a `tools.restrict` allow list — add `save_workspace_memory` to that list if so.

## Installation

The package is plain JavaScript with no build step, so every install channel works:

```sh
# from npm (once published)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-workspace-memories

# straight from GitHub (no build script needed — sources ship as-is)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lengfengng-tech/dsh-workspace-memories

# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-workspace-memories
```

Or use the GUI: sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste a package name, GitHub address, or absolute local path, then **Enable now**.

Uninstall: the Plugins page, or `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-workspace-memories`.

## Usage

- Open the **Workspace Memory** entry in the sidebar. The selector defaults to the workspace of the current session. **New file** creates a `.md` memory (the extension is added when missing); select a file to edit, save, or delete it.
- Tell the agent "remember: this project uses pnpm, not npm" — it writes a memory file that every session of the workspace (and the panel) sees immediately.
- Storage and layout are configurable: `storage: home` (default, DSH data directory, outside the project) or `storage: workspace` (inside the project at `directory`, default `.dsh/memory`).

## Important: start a new session after installing or upgrading

Tool registration takes effect immediately on the host, but **a model's visible tool list is assembled when each conversation turn starts**:

- If a session's current turn began *before* the plugin was installed or reloaded, that turn's tool declaration is stale. This is most visible in **PTC mode**, where the model reads a pre-generated TypeScript binding (`ToolArgsMap`) that does not yet contain `save_workspace_memory` — the model may conclude "there is no memory tool", or fall back to probing the tool by name through the code channel (which actually works, since dispatch goes through the live host registry).
- **The fix is simple: start a new session, or just send a new message after the current turn ends.** The next turn regenerates the tool declaration and `save_workspace_memory` appears normally — no probing needed.

Memory injection into the system prompt is attached when an agent is created (session start, resume after a restart, clear, or compaction); once attached, a session picks up changed memory files on its next step automatically.

## Data layout and safety

Two storage modes, chosen by the plugin's `storage` config:

| Mode | Memory location | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `home` (default) | `~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace-key>/` — outside the project | Machine-local or sensitive notes: server configs, environment quirks, personal conventions |
| `workspace` | `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` — inside the project | Team-shared memories meant to be committed alongside the code |

```
~/.dsh/workspace-memory/     # default memory store, one subdirectory per workspace
dsh-workspace-memories/        # this plugin
├── package.json             #   bundle manifest (dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client)
├── cordis.patch.yml         #   plugin row declaration
├── index.js                 #   host: /api routes + prompt injection + the save tool
├── client.js                #   browser: sidebar entry + management panel
├── locale/                  #   panel copy (en, zh)
├── icon.svg
└── selftest.mjs             #   host-logic self-test: node selftest.mjs
```

Safety constraints: the browser panel can only address registered workspaces by `workspaceId` (no arbitrary host paths); file names are strictly validated (no path separators, `..`, whitespace, or control characters); one file is capped at 1 MiB; prompt injection truncates each file to 32K characters and caps at 20 files.

## Development

- Install with a `link:` dependency (local-path install does this): editing `client.js` hot-reloads in the page via the client HMR receiver; editing `index.js` (host code) requires a DSH restart to load the new module generation.
- Run the self-test: `node selftest.mjs` (mocks the plugin context; covers routes, prompt rendering, tool writes, and validation failures).
- Runtime checks: host entry `include:workspace-memory` should be `active`; the client slot `sidebar.panellist` should list a `workspace-memory` occupant; `save_workspace_memory` should appear in the tool list.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) — © 2026 lengfengng-tech

---

This is a community plugin built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness); it is not an official DeepSeek product. Naming follows the [DSH brand guidelines](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/BRAND_GUIDELINES.md).

plugins.description: MCP Master for DeepSeek Harness: per-session MCP server picker with global and project (.mcp.json) catalogs, OAuth sign-in, and trust review
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-master

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**MCP Master for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).** Choose which MCP servers each session uses — from your **global** list and the workspace's **project** list — with a picker that sits right before the composer's model selector. Pick them when a session starts, and switch them at any time afterwards, just like the model.

- **Project servers** come from the files other agents already use: `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.dsh/mcp.json`.
- **Global servers** come from `~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json` (same `mcpServers` format). A project server shadows a global one of the same name.

```json
// <workspace>/.mcp.json  or  ~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "orion-mcp":            { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--project", ".", "orion-mcp"] },
    "atlassian-mcp-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2" },
    "conduktor-console":    { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "https://…/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer ${CONDUKTOR_API_TOKEN}"], "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

## The picker

`[ 🔌 MCP 2 ● ]  [ model ▾ ]  [ ➤ ]` — in the composer row of every session, including a brand-new one.

- **Zero footprint when unused**: no global or project servers → nothing renders.
- **Chip**: number of servers active in this session and one status dot for them (green connected · amber sign-in needed · red failing · pulsing starting). A small blue dot means project servers await review.
- **Panel** (click the chip; Esc / click outside to close): *Project* and *Global* groups. Each row has a **checkbox = use in this session**, status, transport, a `default` tag, and inline **Sign in** / **Retry**. Expand a row for the command/URL (as written — never variable-expanded), auth, server version, tools, logs, Reconnect, Sign out, Revoke trust.
- **Footer**: what new sessions start with, and **Use for new sessions** to save the current selection as this workspace's default (**Reset** returns to the files' own `enabled` flags).
- Theme tokens only (light/dark follow the app); copy follows **Settings → General → Language**.

## How sessions get servers

| Topic | Behavior |
|---|---|
| New session | Starts from the workspace default: the saved one, or else every trusted server whose file entry is not `"enabled": false` / `"disabled": true`. |
| Forks & subagents | Inherit the parent session's selection (`parentSession`). |
| Switching later | Checking/unchecking registers/unregisters that server's tools in **this session only**, from the next step on. DSH itself records tool additions/removals in the session log (`developer/message` tool-addition/removal), so history, resume, and replay stay consistent — unlike an agent preset, which is a whole plugin composition and therefore locked once the session starts. |
| Persistence | Selections, defaults, trust, and OAuth tokens live in `~/.dsh/mcp-master/state.json` (0600). Config files are never modified. |
| Process lifetime | A server runs while a live session — or a session open in the UI but not started yet — selects it; it stops 2 minutes after the last one deselects it, and a workspace with no sessions or viewers shuts down after 15 idle minutes. |

## Trust (project servers)

A `.mcp.json` in a cloned repository can run any command, so project servers must be **trusted** before they run (same model as Claude Code's project-server approval). Checking an untrusted server shows the exact command/URL with **Trust & use**. Trust is per workspace and bound to the entry as written: if the command, args, env, URL, or headers change, the server becomes **Changed** and needs review again. Global servers are yours and always trusted. `autoTrust: true` skips the review.

## Transports and auth

- **stdio** (own process group, reaped with its children; cwd = workspace root), **Streamable HTTP** (session ids, SSE responses, `list_changed` stream), **legacy HTTP+SSE** (automatic fallback). Server→client `ping` / `roots/list` are answered.
- **OAuth** per the MCP authorization spec: RFC 9728 → RFC 8414/OIDC discovery → RFC 7591 dynamic client registration → authorization code + PKCE (S256) with RFC 8707 `resource`, then refresh. Tokens are keyed by server URL, so one sign-in covers every workspace. An explicit `Authorization` header is used as-is; `"oauth": { "clientId", "clientSecret", "scope" }` covers providers without dynamic registration.
- **Variables**: `${VAR}`, `${VAR:-default}`, `${env:VAR}`, `${workspaceFolder}` — resolved from DSH's environment layered over your login-shell environment (so `~/.zshrc` exports and your shell `PATH` work in the desktop app).
- **Tools** are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>` like the built-in MCP client; input schemas are folded into the registry's JSON-Schema subset (`$ref`, nullable `anyOf`, type arrays, `allOf`; dropped constraints become description hints); `readOnlyHint` tools may run in parallel.

## Configuration (optional)

```yaml
# your profile's cordis.patch.yml
- id: mcp-master
  name: dsh-mcp-master
  config:
    globalConfigFile: ~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json   # false disables the global scope
    configFiles: [.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .dsh/mcp.json]
    autoTrust: false
    searchParents: true          # also look in parent directories of the session cwd
    startupWaitMs: 5000          # a new session waits this long for selected servers that are still starting
    connectTimeoutMs: 60000
    toolCallTimeoutMs: 300000
    idleShutdownMinutes: 15
```

## Security notes

- `/mcp-master/api/*` passes DSH's connection fence (Host/Origin + browser authentication); mutating calls also need a custom header that cross-origin pages cannot send without a CORS preflight; paths must be inside registered workspaces or live session directories.
- The OAuth redirect (`/mcp-master/oauth/callback`) opens in your system browser without the DSH cookie and is authorized by a single-use 192-bit `state`.
- Logs and the UI redact codes, tokens, and `Bearer` values; command lines are shown unexpanded. `state.json` holds tokens — treat it like a credentials file.

## Develop

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run verify          # build + typecheck + tests (node --test runs the .ts tests directly)
```

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | Host entry: options, agent lifecycle hooks, route mounting |
| `src/host/config.ts` | Catalog discovery (project + global), dialects, variable expansion, fingerprints |
| `src/host/runtime.ts` | Trust, defaults, per-session selections, server lifecycle, per-agent tool registration |
| `src/host/state.ts` | Persistent state (`~/.dsh/mcp-master/state.json`) |
| `src/host/stdio.ts`, `http.ts`, `jsonrpc.ts` | MCP transports and JSON-RPC plumbing (zero runtime dependencies) |
| `src/host/oauth.ts` | MCP authorization (discovery, DCR, PKCE, refresh) |
| `src/host/schema.ts`, `tools.ts` | Schema folding and ToolDefinitions |
| `src/host/api.ts` | HTTP API + OAuth callback |
| `src/client/*` | Composer picker (React; `__ModuleLoader__` bundle; portal popover like the model menu) |
| `src/shared/types.ts` | Wire contract between the halves |

After rebuilding an installed copy, restart DSH: the Host module is an ES module and is not re-imported in place.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: 在 DeepSeek Harness 的每条回复下面加一行：本次问答花了多少钱 + 账户余额（充值/礼金分开列，没有礼金就只显示充值余额）。鼠标悬停时显示饼图。按该轮 token 用量乘官方峰谷单价计算，内置节假日表；算不出价就写明原因，不静默出错。插件自身不联网（余额由 dsh 宿主查询）、不落盘、无依赖。
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-cost-receipt [![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/divineeagleblackhand/dsh-cost-receipt) 在 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（dsh）每条回复下面加一行：**本次问答花了多少钱**，以及账户余额。鼠标悬停可看费用构成的饼图，按花费占比画。 ``` 本次问答花费 ¥0.165824 账户余额 ¥6.2164 礼金余额 ¥1.5366 ``` ## 特点 - **按"一问一答"计价**：每条回复下面一行，看的是刚才这一问花了多少。历史轮次也有数字，按它当时的时段定价，打开旧会话照样算得出来。 - **余额拆成两个数**：`账户余额`只算充值余额，`礼金余额`另起一项，相加才是钱包总额。没有礼金时第二项不显示。余额只出现在每条对话的最新一轮（历史轮次显示当时的钱没有意义）。 - **悬停看费用构成**：本次问答与整场对话**并排两个环，按花费占比画**，不是 token 占比。因为缓存命中的 token 通常占 99%，却只占不到四成花费；按 token 画会退化成一个看不见的细弧。 - **算不出价就写明原因**，绝不静默出错：角标会直接写 `未收录模型 xxx`、`混用多模型（a + b）`、`用量未标注模型`。拿别的模型的单价硬套会错好几倍，而且看不出来。 - **角标上的时刻表示"未变"，不是"刚读过"**：宿主会缓存账号查询，所以那个 `HH:MM:SS` 是**余额上次变化的时刻** —— 时刻不动＝数字没再变过。鼠标悬停还能看到**最后一次查询时刻**，两个一对比就知道是读数陈旧、还是余额真的没动。 ## 安装 从 npm 装（推荐：名字短，还能锁版本）： ``` dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-cost-receipt ``` 或直接从 GitHub 仓库装： ``` dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/divineeagleblackhand/dsh-cost-receipt ``` 也可以在 dsh 插件页的「添加插件」里粘上面任意一条地址（桌面版的 profile 名就是 `desktop`）。 装完刷新页面。若角标没出现，完全退出并重启桌面版。 > 若直连 GitHub 困难，用 npm 那条命令；或先把仓库克隆到本地，再用绝对路径安装。 ## 隐私与联网 - **插件自身不直接联网**：`client.js` / `index.js` 里没有任何 `fetch`、`XMLHttpRequest`、WebSocket 调用，可以逐行核对。 - **余额经由宿主查询**：插件通过 dsh 宿主的 `account/getBalance` 取余额（和你打开账号设置看到的是同一条路径），因此**每 30 秒会触发一次账号查询，页面不可见时降为每 3 分钟一次**。这是它唯一与外部有关的动作，走的是 dsh 自带的账号功能，账号令牌始终只在宿主手里。 - **零存储**：不写任何文件，不用 localStorage。 - **零凭据访问**：不读 API Key，不读任何配置文件。 - 唯一读取的本地数据是当前会话的 token 用量，也就是 dsh 自己「本轮用量」面板用的那一份。 > 仓库里的 `tools/fetch-holidays.mjs` 是**维护脚本**，用来刷新内置的节假日表：它需要联网（默认查第三方节假日 API，也可传入国务院通知原文的 URL 做交叉校验），由维护者**一年手动跑一次**，而且**不会随 npm 包发布给用户**（打包白名单 `files` 里只有插件运行必需的那几个文件）。 ## 计价口径与边界 | 项 | 口径 | |---|---| | 一轮 | 一次问答：一条用户消息 → 最终回复 | | 计价 | 缓存命中输入 / 未缓存输入 / 缓存写入 / 输出 四桶分别乘单价。缓存写入按未命中输入计价（官方没有单独的缓存写入价） | | 单价 | 人民币 / 百万 token，按模型分开，取自官方价目表 | | 时段 | 高峰＝北京时间周一至周五 9:00–12:00、14:00–18:00，**不含法定节假日**，其余时间空闲价。判定与你的系统时区无关 | | 节假日 | 内置国务院 2026 年安排（19 天）。未收录的年份退回"不修正"，不会给错答案，只是不再修正 | | 币种 | **只支持人民币账户**。检测到非人民币钱包时一个金额都不显示，只提示「仅支持人民币账户」 | 已知误差： - **跨峰谷边界的轮次**按该轮结束时刻整轮定价，最坏偏 50%（一轮 5 分钟跨界的概率约 1.4%）。 - **整场累计**只覆盖已加载进视图的轮次；超长会话分页时这个数会偏低。 - **单价表与节假日表会随官方更新**，需要手动改常量（见下）。 ## 兼容性 - 需要 **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2**：插件依赖它内部的 turn-tail 数据与 account Remote。dsh 升级后如果角标消失，第一个要怀疑的就是这里。 - Web 版与桌面版均可，Windows 与 macOS 均可（纯客户端插件，不碰文件系统，也没有平台分支）。 - 非人民币账户不显示金额（见上）。 ## 开发 ``` npm test ``` 测试脚本会**从 `client.js` 里切片抽出真实的计价代码来执行**，而不是复制一份——避免"测的和跑的不是同一份"。覆盖：峰谷时段边界、节假日、三项拆解对账、饼图与角标同源、会话累计、悬停面板结构、币种判定、中英字典对齐。 - 改价格表：`client.js` 顶部的 `PRICES` - 刷新节假日表：`node tools/fetch-holidays.mjs <年份>`（可再传国务院通知原文 URL 做交叉校验） ## 许可 MIT --- **English** — A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugin that adds one line under every reply showing what that exchange cost, priced from the turn's own token usage at the official peak/off-peak CNY rates, together with the account and bonus balances. Hover for a cost breakdown of the exchange versus the whole conversation. When a price cannot be computed it says why instead of guessing. The plugin makes no network calls of its own — the balance is read through the dsh host, which is also how dsh's own account page reads it; it stores nothing and never touches credentials. Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2; CNY accounts only.

plugins.description: Shrink the DeepSeek Harness skill catalog from O(n) to ~600 tokens - router + on-demand category indexes. Zero dependencies, cross-platform.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-skill-router

![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-blue)
![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)
![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-success)
![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/mikuniemo/dsh-skill-router)

**Turn the DeepSeek Harness skill catalog from O(all skills) into one ~600-token router.**

DSH publishes every skill's `name` + `description` into `<available_skills>` in **every request**.
That is invisible until you have a real library — then it is fatal:

| skills resident | catalog cost / request |
|---:|---:|
| 50 | ~5,000 tok |
| 1,246 (measured, real library) | **~70,800 tok** |

On a 200K context that is **35% gone before your first message**; on 128K you are over budget before
you start. The catalog is cached, so it is not a *billing* problem — it is a *context* problem.

This tool moves the skills out of the scanned roots, leaves a single `skill-router` skill behind,
and generates per-category index files the model `read`s on demand:

| | resident tokens |
|---|---:|
| before | ~70,800 (measured) |
| after | **~600** |

On-demand cost: one index file, 1–4K tokens, only when the category is needed.

Zero dependencies. Node ≥ 20 (the same floor DSH itself requires). Works on Windows, Linux, macOS.

## Why not just `disable-model-invocation`?

Because it does not do what you want. Per the DSH docs, it removes the skill from model-facing
catalogs **and loaders** — hidden means unloadable. Moving the skill out of the scanned root keeps
it loadable via `read` while removing its catalog cost.

## Install

No install needed — it is a zero-dependency Node script:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mikuniemo/dsh-skill-router.git
cd dsh-skill-router
node bin/dsh-skill-router.mjs --help
```

or run straight from anywhere:

```bash
npx github:mikuniemo/dsh-skill-router --help
```

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. See the truth: every root DSH scans, what the catalog costs,
#    and the skills DSH silently skips (bad frontmatter).
dsh-skill-router scan

# 2. Preview the plan. Writes nothing.
dsh-skill-router plan --source "D:\my-skills" --locale zh

# 3. Apply: link skills into the off-root, write router + indexes.
dsh-skill-router apply --source "D:\my-skills" --locale zh

# 4. Prove every index path resolves.
dsh-skill-router verify

# 5. Undo everything. Source libraries are never touched.
dsh-skill-router restore
```

### Multi-library example (the author's setup)

```bash
dsh-skill-router apply \
  --source "D:\daily\skill_merged\skills" \
  --source "D:\resource\Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills\skills" \
  --exclude-file excluded.json \
  --overrides category-map.json \
  --locale zh
```

`--source` is repeatable. Any directory whose immediate children are skill bundles
(`<name>/SKILL.md` or `<name>.md`) works.

## How it works

```
~/.dsh/skills/            ← scanned root. ONLY skill-router lives here.
  └── skill-router/SKILL.md     (~600 tokens: the table below)

~/.dsh/skill-index/       ← NOT scanned by DSH. Ordinary markdown.
  ├── ctf.md                    "- **ctf-crypto** — …\n  `D:\…\ctf-crypto\SKILL.md`"
  ├── malware-analysis.md
  └── skill-manager.md          (meta-skill: how to add/remove/find skills)

~/.dsh/skills-off/        ← the real skills, one junction/symlink per skill,
  ├── ctf-crypto  ──────────→  D:\daily\skill_merged\skills\ctf-crypto
  └── …                            (source libraries stay where they are)
```

The model loads a skill in three hops: read router → read one index → read one SKILL.md.

## The five design decisions (and the evidence behind them)

These were all learned the hard way against real libraries. They are the reason this
tool exists rather than a 20-line PowerShell script.

### 1. Links go into the off-root, never the scanned root

The naive flow — "put real directories in `~/.dsh/skills`, then move them out with
`-DisableSkills`" — **produces dead index paths**. The index records
`<skillsRoot>/<name>/SKILL.md`; the very next step moves that directory away; the
router then advertises skills that do not exist. (Reproduced and reported upstream.)

This tool never moves anything. It creates **junctions (Windows) / symlinks (POSIX)
pointing at your source libraries**, and the indexes record the *target* paths, which
never move. Deleting a link never touches the target. `~/.dsh` can be wiped and
reinstalled without losing a single skill.

### 2. One scan root is never enough

DSH scans **five** roots (rank 100 project-dsh → 500 user-agents). A tool that only
manages `~/.dsh/skills` (rank 400) silently ignores rank 100/200/300/500 — and any
skill still resident there keeps costing tokens. `scan` shows all five, including
`customSkillDirs` parsed from your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.

### 3. Discovery is one level deep — mirror it exactly

DSH recognises `<root>/<name>/SKILL.md` and `<root>/<name>.md`; nested `**/SKILL.md`
is **deliberately not discovered**. This tool mirrors that exactly, so what it counts
is what DSH counts — no surprises when a nested skill "doesn't show up".

It also handles the two real-world shapes that make a skill **silently invisible** to
DSH (the provider skips the whole skill with only a log warning):

- a UTF-8 **BOM** before the opening `---`
- a `/* ... */` **comment banner** before the frontmatter (14 skills in the author's
  library were dead this way)

`scan` lists every such skill and tells you the two-line fix.

### 4. A classifier is only as good as its budget

The obvious classifier — `subdomain` frontmatter, else name prefix, else `other` —
put **489 of 1,548 skills** into one bucket on a real library, producing a single
~25,100-token index file. The router would then cost as much as the catalog it
replaced.

So classification here is budget-driven, not taxonomy-driven:

- signals, in priority order: `--overrides` map → `metadata.category` → `subdomain`
  → name prefix → `other`
- any bucket over `--max-tokens` (default 4000) is **split** — first by the most
  discriminative token in skill names (max 2 levels), then unconditionally by
  alphabetical binning, which packs by measured tokens and always converges
- buckets that are tiny fold into `other` so the router table stays small
- duplicate bucket names are de-duplicated (`-2`, `-3`…) so two halves of one split
  can never overwrite each other's index file

Measured on the author's library: 60 buckets, **0 over budget**, largest exactly 4000 tokens.

### 5. Token math must be honest

Two mistakes this tool refuses to make:

- **counting raw descriptions.** DSH caps each description at
  `catalogDescriptionMaxLength` (default 500). Uncapped math overstates by ~3%
  (measured 595,650 vs 578,548 chars). We model the cap.
- **assuming ~4 chars/token for everything.** That is fine for English and badly
  wrong for CJK, where one character is often one token. Token estimates here are
  script-aware.

## Commands

| command | what it does | writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `scan` | all five roots, resident catalog cost, silently-skipped skills | no |
| `plan` | categories, index sizes, link actions | no |
| `apply` | create links, write router + indexes + manifest | yes (`--dry-run` supported) |
| `verify` | fail (exit 1) if any index path is dead; flag catalog re-inflation | no |
| `restore` | remove our links and generated files only | source libraries untouched |

Useful flags: `--source` (repeatable) · `--exclude <name|prefix*>` · `--exclude-file <json>`
· `--overrides <json>` · `--max-tokens <n>` · `--locale <zh|en>` · `--profile <name>`
· `--dsh-home <dir>` · `--dry-run` · `--json`

## Rolling it out on another machine

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mikuniemo/dsh-skill-router.git
cd dsh-skill-router
node bin/dsh-skill-router.mjs scan              # see what you have
node bin/dsh-skill-router.mjs plan --source <your-skill-library> --locale zh
node bin/dsh-skill-router.mjs apply --source <your-skill-library> --locale zh
node bin/dsh-skill-router.mjs verify
# restart DSH to be safe (the watcher usually picks it up live)
```

Rollback: `restore` (or just delete `skills/skill-router`,

plugins.description: 把 Hindsight 编码插件的 bank 身份锚定到远程仓库名，而不是本地目录名。Anchors Hindsight coding-agent memory banks to the remote repository name instead of the local directory name.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-hindsight-bank-router **把 Hindsight 编码插件的 bank 身份锚定到「远程仓库名」而不是「本地目录名」——让同一仓库的每个克隆都共享同一个记忆库** [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.0--rc.2%20实测-4c6ef5)](#) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm%20test-42%20passed-2ea043)](#自测) [![runtime deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/运行时依赖-0-8a8f99)](#它怎么做) [![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/j62268781-alt/dsh-hindsight-bank-router)
--- `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` 给每个仓库一份长期记忆，但 bank 名取自**本地目录名**：同一个仓库因各人 `git clone` 得到不同目录名而分叉成互不相通的记忆库，**且完全静默**。本插件喂给它一份动态生成的 `mapPathToBank`，把身份锚定到远程仓库名。 - 🎯 **锚定远程仓库名**：`payments-app`（本地名）与 `mobile-client`（远程名）都解析到 `git::mobile-client`，团队记忆真正汇合 - 🪜 **声明式优先级链**：用户级工作区文件 → 仓库内 `.hindsight.json` → git 远程名 → 目录名；显式配置永远最高优先 - 🔐 **两把锁才生效**：用户级 `enableBankRouter` **必须显式写 true**，加上部署级开关。任一为假就彻底不动你的配置 - 🛡️ **绝不覆盖你手写的映射**：sidecar 状态文件记录"我管理过哪些路径"，删除时只动自己写的那些 - 🚫 **不 spawn git**：直接读 `.git/config` —— 无子进程、无超时、不会因机器负载失败（上游为此删过一版 spawn 实现，见 [#3950](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/issues/3950)） - 🈶 **中文仓库名可用**：先 `decodeURIComponent` 再清理，`中文仓库.git` → `git::中文仓库`（顺序反了会变 `-E4-B8-AD` 乱码） - 🧯 **失败开放**：任何异常只记日志，绝不阻断 DSH 启动或会话 **目录**：[它解决什么问题](#它解决什么问题) · [安装](#安装) · [配置](#配置) · [路由规则](#路由规则优先级链) · [安全承诺](#安全承诺) · [已知限制](#已知限制) · [更多文档](#更多文档) · [License](#license) ## 它解决什么问题 `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` 的 bank 名来自模板 `coding-agent::{gitProject}`，而 `{gitProject}` 的解析逻辑（源码 `core/bank.ts` 的 `resolveProjectRoot`）是： ```ts if (basename(commonDir) === ".git") return { root: dirname(commonDir) }; // {gitProject} = basename(root) ``` **它只读磁盘上的目录名，从不读 `remote.origin.url`。** 后果是同一个仓库因各人 `git clone` 得到的目录名不同而分叉： ``` 你: git clone → payments-app → coding-agent::payments-app 同事: git clone → mobile-client → coding-agent::mobile-client ``` 两者都"正常工作"，**记忆却永不交汇，且完全静默**——没有任何日志提示你出了问题。 上游把这种静默分叉视为最严重的失败模式（见 `git-layout.ts` 注释与 issue #3950），但它的防护只覆盖了 linked worktree，没覆盖"同一仓库、不同本地目录名"。 ## 它怎么做 不动 hindsight 插件本身，只喂给它一份**动态生成的 `mapPathToBank`**： ``` DSH 启动 └─ 本插件 apply() ├─ 扫描配置的根目录，找 .git ├─ 直接解析 .git/config 的 remote.origin.url ← 绝不 spawn git ├─ 由远程 URL 推导 bank 名：git:: └─ 安全合并进 ~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json 的 mapPathToBank ↓ hindsight 插件首次会话时惰性解析 bank → 读到的就是正确的映射 ``` **可行性依据**（hindsight 源码）：`readRaw()` 每次调用都 `readFileSync` 重新读文件、**没有缓存**，而 `workspaceFor(root)` 是**首次会话才构建**的。所以只要在同一个进程的加载期写入，就一定先于它的读取。 ### 为什么不 spawn git 上游 `git-layout.ts` 明确记录了删除 spawn 实现的原因：`git rev-parse` 带 1000ms 预算，机器繁忙时会超时、进程压力下会 `EAGAIN`，两种失败都被映射为 `null` —— 与"不是仓库"无法区分，于是把 worktree 分叉进自己的 bank（#3950）。 直接读 `.git/config` 是纯文件读取：**无子进程、无超时、不会因负载失败**。 ## 路由规则：优先级链 插件为每个工作区决定 bank 名，**严格按以下顺序**，第一个命中者胜出： ``` ① <用户目录>/workspaces/<目录名>.json 的 bankId ← 用户自己控制，最高优先 ② <工作区>/.hindsight.json 的 bankId ← 仓库自带（可关闭） ③ git 仓库 → git::<远程仓库名> ← 锚定客观身份，团队共享 ④ git 仓库但无 origin ← 不生成映射，交回默认 ⑤ 非 git 目录 → workspace::<目录名> ← 个人记忆（可关闭） ``` **注意 ①② 与 ③⑤ 的关系**：显式配置（①②）**无论是否 git 仓库都优先**——它是"我知道得比你多"的逃生舱。 ### 总览图 ``` 扫描根目录 ├─ 有 .hindsight.json？ → 用它的 bankId（①②） ├─ 是 git 仓库？ → 读 remote.origin.url │ ├─ 有 origin → git::<远程名> ✅ 锚定远端 │ └─ 无 origin → 不写映射 ⚠️ 交回默认 └─ 非 git 目录？ → workspace::<目录名> （routeNonGit 控制） ``` ### ① 开关：两把锁 路由默认**关闭**，需要**两个开关同时为真**： | 位置 | 字段 | 作用 | |---|---|---| | `~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json` | `"enableBankRouter": true` | **用户级总闸** | | `cordis.patch.yml` 的 config | `enabled: true` | 部署级开关（DSH profile 控制） | **任一为假就彻底不动你的配置。** 用户级开关必须**显式写 true**（不是"缺省即开"），因为它是会改写你配置文件的动作，应当由你主动授权。 ### ② 显式指定：`.hindsight.json` 在**两处**查找，**用户级优先**： | 位置 | 谁控制 | 优先级 | |---|---|---| | `~/.hindsight/workspaces/<目录名>.json` | **你** | 高 | | `<工作区>/.hindsight.json` | 仓库 | 低 | 两种字段写法都接受： ```jsonc { "bankId": "custom::my-bank" } // 推荐 { "bank": "custom::my-bank" } // 兼容 hindsight 的 banks..bank 用词 ``` **为什么用户级优先**：上游明确反对仓库携带配置—— > There is no per-repo opt-in file, for the same reason there is no repo-carried config at all: **a cloned repository must not be able to turn memory on.** 理由是一个克隆下来的仓库不应能决定你的记忆行为。本插件保留仓库级配置是为团队随仓库统一 bank 命名的便利，但**用户级永远压过它**：仓库想改你的 bank，你在用户级写一条就能推翻。 完全不接受该风险时，在 `cordis.patch.yml` 设 `allowRepoConfig: false` 关闭仓库级查找。 ### ③ Git 仓库 → 锚定远程仓库名 **判定**：目录下存在 `.git`（**目录或文件都算**——后者是 linked worktree / submodule）。 **推导链**： ``` .git 存在 ↓ resolveCommonGitDir() ← worktree 感知，只读文件、不 spawn git ↓ 读 /config ↓ remoteUrlFromConfig() ← 只认 [remote "origin"] 段的 url ↓ bankNameFromRemote(url, "git::") ↓ 写入 mapPathToBank[仓库路径] = "git::<仓库名>" ``` **URL → bank 名的完整规则**（取 URL 的**最后一段路径**，而非本地目录名）： | 输入 URL | 处理 | bank 名 | |---|---|---| | `https://host/a/b/**mobile-client**.git` | 末段去 `.git` | `git::mobile-client` | | `git@github.com:org/**repo**.git` | scp 风格先拆出 path | `git::repo` | | `ssh://git@host/a/**repo**` | 取 URL pathname | `git::repo` | | `https://host/a/**my%20repo**.git` | **先解码**再把空格转 `-` | `git::my-repo` | | `https://host/a/**中文仓库**.git` | 解码后 CJK 原样保留 | `git::中文仓库` | ⚠️ **解码顺序很重要**：`new URL()` 会把空格转成 `%20`、把中文转成 `%E4%B8%AD…`，因此实现**必须先用 `decodeURIComponent` 解码，再做字符清理**。若顺序反了，`my repo` 会变成 `my-20repo`、中文仓库名会变成 `-E4-B8-AD…` 乱码。 字符白名单用 Unicode 属性 `[\p{L}\p{N}_.-]`（而非 `\w`），中文/日文/韩文仓库名因此能原样保留。空仓库名或清理后为空的情况返回 `null`（不生成映射）。 **实例**（本机实测）： ``` ~/work/payments-app → git::mobile-client ← 锚定成功 ~/work/web-console → git::web-console ~/work/flutter → git::flutter ``` 注意第一条：本地目录叫 `payments-app`，但远程仓库名是 `mobile-client`，**插件取的是后者**。 **特殊处理**： - **linked worktree** —— `.git` 是文件（内容 `gitdir: …/worktrees/`）时，读其 `commondir` 回溯到**主仓库**。结果：worktree 与主仓库映射到**同一个 bank**，在哪个分支工作都共享记忆。 - **无 `origin` 远程地址** —— **不生成映射**，只记一条 debug 日志（`无 origin 远程地址 —— 保持默认 bank 命名`）。没有远程地址就无法推导稳定身份，此时**交回 hindsight 默认逻辑**（用目录名），而不是猜一个。这符合上游"宁可跳过也不猜"的原则。 ### ④ 非 Git 目录 → workspace::<目录名> **默认接管**（`routeNonGit: true`）：为根目录的**直接子目录**写 `workspace::<目录名>`。 ``` ~/Documents/Qoder → workspace::Qoder ``` **为什么接管而不是放任**：hindsight 默认会给它 `coding-agent::Qoder`，与团队共享的 `git::*` 混在同一命名空间里，**无法一眼区分"这是个人记忆还是团队知识"**。用独立前缀把它们分开。 **只处理根目录的直接子目录**，不递归为任意深度的目录建映射——否则会产出大量无意义的 bank。 **关掉它**（`routeNonGit: false`）：不生成映射，让这些目录走 hindsight 默认的 `coding-agent::<目录名>`。 ### ⑤ 为什么这样分工 | | git 仓库 | 非 git 目录 | |---|---|---| | 身份锚点 | **远程 URL**（客观、人人一致） | 目录名（主观、因人而异） | | 团队共享 | ✅ **有意义**（同事 clone 同一仓库） | ❌ 无意义（个人工作区） | | bank 前缀 | `git::` | `workspace::` | | 归谁管 | 锚定远端，修正分叉 | 显式接管，命名空间隔离 | **核心判断**：git 仓库有"客观身份"可锚定（修掉静默分叉）；非 git 目录没有，所以用独立前缀**明确标记为个人记忆**，而不是假装它有团队身份。 ### ⑥ 一条边界情况 **递归扫描时发现仓库就停止向下**（`return`）： ``` ~/Documents/ ├── my-monorepo/ ← 有 .git，建映射后停止递归 │ └── packages/a/ ← 不再深入（即使它自己也是 git 仓库） └── other/ ← 继续扫描 ``` **理由**：仓库内嵌套仓库极罕见，且会把扫描成本放大。 ### ⚠️ 已知边界：非 git 目录的 bank 名仍是目录名 这意味着**不同人机器上的同名目录会撞到同一个 bank**（若都连同一台服务器）： ``` 你的 Mac: ~/Documents/output → coding-agent::output 同事 Mac: ~/Documents/output → coding-agent::output ← 撞车 ``` **本插件不处理这种情况**（它只认 git 仓库）。需要时用 `mapPathToBank` 手工映射——插件**绝不碰你手写的条目**（见下方安全承诺）。 ## 安全承诺 这个插件会写你的配置文件，所以约束是它的核心： | 承诺 | 实现 | |---|---| | **绝不覆盖用户手工写的映射** | sidecar state 文件记录"我管理过哪些路径"；删除时只有值仍等于我当初写的值才动手 | | **无变化不写盘** | 合并结果与现状相同则完全不动文件，避免 mtime 抖动触发文件监视 | | **失败开放** | 任何异常只记日志，绝不阻断 DSH 启动或会话 | | **原子写入** | 临时文件 + plugins.readme_text:
# StateDock Plugins

**Agents come and go. Tasks remain.**

Shared Skills and lightweight plugin packages for [StateDock](https://statedock.dev): save a plan, restore task context, and record progress across coding tools. All packages connect to the existing StateDock Remote MCP service. This repository contains client instructions and packaging only.

> Version 0.1.1 adds structured Git Code Reference guidance to task pickup and completion. Codex local marketplace installation and authenticated remote connectivity have been verified. DeepSeek Harness and ChatGPT distributions at 0.1.0 remain the published/submitted versions; updated 0.1.1 packages are prepared locally and have not been published or resubmitted.

## What you can do

| Skill | Purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `statedock-plan` | Save a deferred idea as PLAN or preserve its discussion and decisions | Does not start implementation |
| `statedock-pickup` | Restore a task's context; explicitly claim one assigned READY task when authorized | Returns context and stops after one pickup |
| `statedock-update` | Record supplied progress, blockers, or a verified completion handoff | Does not perform the work being reported |

The plugin does not execute task code, launch agents, run background polling, schedule work, or orchestrate agents. Your coding host performs implementation under your instructions. Setting a task to READY does not wake an agent.

Example requests:

- “Save a plan to add export support to this project. Do not start it.”
- “Restore the context for SD-000123 without changing its status.”
- “Claim one READY task assigned to my identity and show its context. Do not implement it.”
- “Record these verified results as the handoff for SD-000123.”

Skills verify the connected instance and the repository's project binding before writing. They use live tool schemas and stop if the required tools or binding are missing. Server records and attachments provide context; they do not grant new execution permission.

## Install in Codex

Requirements: a Codex client with plugin support, Git, and access to StateDock. No local StateDock server is required. Node.js is needed only for development and packaging.

Clone this repository, then register its local marketplace:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/statedock/statedock-plugins.git
cd statedock-plugins
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add statedock@statedock-local
codex plugin list --json
```

The checked-in `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` points directly to `core/`, the maintained portable plugin source. No build or manual cache copying is needed for this local installation. Restart Codex and open a new chat to check that all three Skills are available.

If `codex` is not on your PATH, use your installed CLI's full executable path. On the macOS installation tested here:

```sh
CODEX_BIN="/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex"
"$CODEX_BIN" plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
"$CODEX_BIN" plugin add statedock@statedock-local
```

That app path is installation-specific. See [installation details](docs/install.md) for manual marketplace configuration and standalone MCP alternatives. This repository has not been published to a public plugin marketplace.

### Codex authentication

The plugin's bundled Remote MCP connection uses the host's OAuth flow by default. Install the plugin, authorize StateDock when Codex prompts you, then start a new chat. Do not replace this with a second connection unless you intentionally want a separate token-based setup.

For a standalone Codex MCP connection using a StateDock token, Codex can add the bearer scheme for you. Set the environment variable securely and configure its **name**, not the token itself:

```sh
codex mcp add statedock --url https://statedock.dev/mcp --bearer-token-env-var STATEDOCK_TOKEN
```

Set `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` in the host's secure environment before connecting; keep its value as the raw token without the `Bearer ` prefix. The resulting request header is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In a Codex connection screen, the **Bearer token env var** field takes `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` (the variable name), not `Authorization` and not the token value. If the host instead provides generic custom-header fields, use **Key** `Authorization` and **Value** `Bearer <token>`. Never commit a real token or paste one into shared files. OAuth and a manually configured bearer token are alternative authentication methods.

## Authenticate and check the connection

The bundled server configuration is:

```text
Endpoint:  https://statedock.dev/mcp
Transport: streamable-http (Agent Plugins format)
```

Complete OAuth in the host's connection UI when requested. Keep existing authorizations while testing; a new plugin connection may still require its own consent. Installing a plugin does not prove that authentication is complete.

Start with this read-only request:

> Call StateDock get_instance_info and report publicOrigin, mcpUrl and transport. Do not create or claim any tasks.

Expected result:

```json
{
  "publicOrigin": "https://statedock.dev",
  "mcpUrl": "https://statedock.dev/mcp",
  "transport": "remote"
}
```

Then confirm the project UUID and its repository path. For READY pickup, the credential must be bound to the intended StateDock Agent Identity. A plugin name or token label does not establish identity.

Never commit tokens or send them in chat. OAuth credentials stay in the host. For a separate standalone Codex connection, [configuration templates](templates/) show OAuth or a securely supplied environment variable. Avoid configuring duplicate StateDock connections; inspect each connection's instance information before use.

## Platform introductions and installation

StateDock provides the same three workflows on hosts that support the shared Agent Plugins package: save a deferred plan, restore task context, and record progress or a verified handoff. The integration stores and restores task state; it does not run code, launch agents, schedule work, or orchestrate agents. Installability and review status differ by platform:

| Platform | What the integration provides | Current distribution and install path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Codex** | Shared plan, pickup, and update Skills plus StateDock Remote MCP. | Install from this repository's local marketplace using the commands above. This has been verified in an isolated Codex CLI profile. It is not a public Codex Marketplace listing. |
| **ChatGPT app** | The same shared Skills and authenticated StateDock MCP connection. | Version 0.1.0 is submitted for review. It will be discoverable in the ChatGPT plugin directory after approval and publication; 0.1.1 is prepared locally but has not been resubmitted. |
| **Cursor** | The shared Agent Plugins package, with no Cursor-specific service code. | Repository marketplace metadata and local-test instructions are present. A real Cursor install and Marketplace listing still need verification; see the [Cursor guide](adapters/cursor/README.md) and [submission notes](docs/cursor-submission.md). |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | Native Cordis Bundle containing the shared Skills; an optional MCP component can connect to StateDock when explicitly enabled. | `@statedock/dsh-plugin@0.1.0` is published on npm. Install with `dsh plugin --profile web add @statedock/dsh-plugin@0.1.0` or use `--profile desktop`. See the [Harness guide](adapters/deepseek-harness/README.md). |
| **Google Antigravity** | Native plugin manifest and remote MCP configuration, packaged with the shared Skills. | The adapter is in this repository at `adapters/antigravity/`. Build and install it locally as described below. Marketplace inclusion requires Google's separate review. |
| **Claude Code** | Planned native manifest and MCP configuration around the shared Skills. | Research notes only; there is no installable Claude Code package yet. |
| **OpenCode** | Planned native MCP connection and shared Skills. | Research notes only; there is no installable OpenCode package yet. |
