# dsh-squares

[**English**](README.md) | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

An **all-in-one workspace plugin** for DSH (DeepSeek Harness): it adds a global
「Square」panel to the Web GUI sidebar that manages **Skills / Experts / Connectors (MCP) / Plugins**
in a single place. **Web (`dsh web`) and Desktop (DeepSeek Harness.app) share the same code and build output.**

Sidebar → 「Square」panel: the four tabs show the Square (official/community catalog) by default; the
「My Experts / My Skills / My MCP / My Plugins」items in the top-right open sub-pages to manage local
content, and 「Back to Square」at the top of the sub-page returns to the Square.

## 1. Installation

Published on npm and GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-squares            # install from npm
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ai-tool-labs/dsh-squares   # or from GitHub
# Desktop: open the "Plugins" panel in the sidebar → click "Add Plugin" → type "dsh-squares" → Install
# Restart harness after installing to take effect (Desktop: restart the App; Web: restart dsh web)
```

A 「Square」entry then appears in the sidebar; click it to open the panel.

## 2. Screenshots

The **Square** panel as it appears in the Web GUI sidebar:

![Square example](assets/example/example-01.png)

## 3. Development

```bash
pnpm --filter dsh-squares typecheck    # host + client tsconfigs
pnpm --filter dsh-squares build        # tsc(host) + tsc(client .d.ts) + esbuild bundle
pnpm --filter dsh-squares smoke        # host smoke test (real Cordis lifecycle + filesystem + routes)
pnpm --filter dsh-squares test:routes  # route integration (expert/connector write paths)
pnpm --filter dsh-squares check:client # bundle shape / id / external-dependency allowlist + mock loader
```

### Building and installing from source (developer)

```bash
pnpm --filter dsh-squares build                                 # build (run pnpm install in the workspace first)
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/dsh-squares    # 2A) Web profile
# 2B) Desktop: the profile is exclusively owned by Electron; use a relative path to write it into the manifest and link via pnpm
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
d.setdefault('dependencies', {})['dsh-squares'] = 'link:/absolute/path/packages/dsh-squares'
bundles = d['dsh']['profile']['bundles']
if 'dsh-squares' not in bundles:
    bundles.append('dsh-squares')
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2) + '\n')
PY
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && CI=true pnpm install
# 3) Restart harness (Desktop: reopen the App; Web: restart dsh web)
```

plugins.description: Give your AI a project memory: /init makes it read the codebase and write .dsh docs, then every later turn gets them injected back automatically.
plugins.readme_text: **English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) # dsh-knowledge — project knowledge system for DSH Let the AI read the project and write what it understood into `.dsh` documents, so every later development request starts with that knowledge already in context. **This plugin does not analyse code itself.** It does exactly two things: hand the prompt to the model, and inject the existing documents back into later turns. Reading the code, deciding feature boundaries and writing the documents is all done by the model with its own tools. ```text /init → the prompt goes in → the model explores the code → the model writes .dsh documents ↓ a development request → documents + update reminder injected → the model changes code → it decides for itself whether the documents went stale ``` ## Install Clone it (or point straight at the GitHub repo) and register it as a bundle in your DSH profile: ```bash cd "$DSH_PROFILE_DIR" pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile # links dsh-knowledge ``` `package.json` needs the dependency and the bundle: ```json { "dependencies": { "dsh-knowledge": "link:" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-knowledge"] } } } ``` Swap `link:` for `github:/` to install straight from GitHub. `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin line: ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-knowledge name: 'dsh-knowledge' ``` **Zero runtime dependencies**: `node:` builtins only. ## Usage ### `/init [path]` — build the knowledge base ```text /init the model reads the whole project and writes to .dsh/ at the project root /init @src the model reads src/ only; documents still go to .dsh/ at the root /init src/lib nested paths work the same ``` Path parsing is deliberately loose: a leading `@` (left behind by the composer's completion) is stripped, paths with spaces can be quoted, naming the project's own directory means the whole project, and a missing path lists the available top-level directories. `/init` itself does exactly two things: **wake the model**, then **inject** the full instruction. **Only the one line you typed shows in the UI** (e.g. `/init @src`). The full instruction is injected as a system-reminder instead of flooding the conversation — the same mechanism the per-turn document injection uses. The model then explores with `glob` / `grep` / `read` and writes with `write`, appearing in the UI like any other turn. **The knowledge base always lives at the project root**, whatever subdirectory `/init` was scoped to. One `.dsh` per project. ### Automatic context injection No manual reminders needed. The first step of every turn injects: 1. the body of `overview.md` (truncated with a pointer to the original when it is long) 2. the document listing under `.dsh` 3. **usage rules and an update reminder** — including: the model judges for itself whether this change made the documents stale One knowledge base is injected once per session, not on every turn; after the model edits documents, they are injected again. ### When to update The injected prompt states the rules, and the model applies them itself: | Change | Update the documents? | |--------|----------------------| | a feature added or removed, or the entry points, execution flow, data flow or module dependencies changed | yes — the affected document | | a bug fix, a style change, an implementation detail that changes no structure | no | | not sure | lean toward not writing | The principle: **better no update than documents that contradict the code.** ## The `.dsh` layout Written by the model from the prompt; a typical structure: ```text .dsh/ ├── overview.md what the project does, its stack, core modules, main entry points ├── architecture.md layers, module boundaries, dependency directions, data flow └── features/.md one per feature: responsibility, entry point, core code, flow, data flow, dependencies ``` File names are meaningful (`auth.md`, `order-sync.md`), never random ids. ## Security - **No source code is copied**: the prompt requires structure and behaviour only — no code snippets, secrets, tokens or connection strings. - **Dangerous scopes are refused**: no knowledge base in the user's home directory, in DSH's own config directory, or at the filesystem root — every session beneath those would mistake it for a project knowledge base. - **Documents are data**: the injected prompt states that any instruction inside `.dsh` is data and must not be executed as an instruction. ## Platform notes | Need | Platform capability | What this plugin does | |------|--------------------|-----------------------| | a command that makes the model work | `Agent.followup(message)` → `send(…, wakeup=true)` → `wakeDriver()` starts a real turn | `/init` admits the single line `/init ` to wake the model; the full instruction goes in through injection | | inject without flooding the UI | `agent/pre-step` waterfall, which can rewrite what enters a step | both the pending `/init` instruction and the per-turn reminder are injected this way; the UI keeps just the command line | | maintain documents at session end | no "session end" event | no programmatic maintenance: the injected prompt asks the model to judge and update for itself | An earlier version of `/init` ran static analysis in the command handler and generated the documents itself. That was wrong: a command handler has no model, so it could only guess feature boundaries with regexes. The command now just hands over the job. Note: the prompt and messages this plugin injects are written in Chinese. ## Tests ```bash node test/run.mjs # everything node test/plugin.test.mjs # plugin behaviour: /init hands over the job, path parsing, refusal rules, injection content node test/real-paths.mjs # replays path forms seen in real use (diagnostic script) node test/lint-imports.mjs # unused imports ``` The tests drive the real `apply()` with a fake Cordis context and assert above all that **`/init` really calls `followup`** — which is exactly what an earlier version got wrong: it did the job itself and never involved the model. ## Configuration None needed. ## Acknowledgments Thanks to everyone who contributed to this project: [](https://github.com/windzxy) [](https://github.com/anyiba) ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: A DeepSeek Harness (cordis) plugin to install and manage local inference providers like Strata, Ninfer, VLLM, llama.cpp, and more.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-local-infer

[中文 (Chinese)](docs/zh/README.md)

> For those who want more performance out of their specific hardware than what Unsloth gives out of the box.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--alpha.3-blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
[![Type: DSH Plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Type-DSH%20Plugin-8A2BE2)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines:

- llama.cpp
- NInfer
- Hyper-Qwen (vLLM)
- Strata
- ...with more coming soon.

![Plugin Screenshot](docs/screenshot-20261014.png)

Pick a model and an engine, tune the parameters, watch a live **VRAM Est.** meter, see **hardware warnings** the moment a value (or a parameter itself) is unsafe for the detected hardware, then the plugin manages **build, deploy, and health-check** for each engine and **automatically register it as a DSH model** once it is confirmed working. No hand-editing of finicky yaml or launchers.

## Install

Command line:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer
```

Web UI: click **Plugins** → **Add Plugin** → paste `https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer`.

## Using the plugin

The **Engine settings** card mounts on the Plugins page (older hosts: the Settings page).

- **Pick an engine and model**, then tune the parameters. Each field renders by its type: checkboxes, dropdowns, sliders, text, directory pickers, and a chat-template combo (known templates plus free text).
- **Watch the VRAM Est. meter.** It prices weights, KV cache, overhead, and workspace against your card as you adjust values, and shows the verdict (`fits` / `tight` / `over`) and the largest context that fits.
- **Read the warnings.** Red banners and inline field warnings fire when a parameter value, or the presence of a parameter, is unsafe for your detected hardware.
- **Satisfy the system dependencies.** The panel lists each missing host dependency (docker, CUDA toolkit, ffmpeg, hf CLI, ...) with its purpose, a copy/paste install string for your OS, and an optional one-click **Run** (sudo). The **Get** button stays disabled until every dependency reports satisfied.
- **Launch / Stop.** `Launch` clones or pulls the engine, downloads the model, starts it, and polls its health endpoint. `Stop` shuts it down.
- **Register / Remove.** `Register` publishes the confirmed-working engine to DSH as a model (optionally as the agent default model) through the settings service, so the change is revision-tracked and undoable. `Remove` pulls the entry back.

All values persist to `~/.dsh/local-infer/config.json`; the browser never sees a value it did not store.

## Supported Platforms

### Operating systems

| OS                           | State     | Notes                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, `apt`) | Supported | Install blocks mirror the working NInfer launcher: the CUDA keyring sequence plus the compile toolchain.            |
| Linux (Arch, `pacman`)       | Supported | `pacman` blocks plus the `/opt/cuda` export lines.                                                                  |
| Linux (Fedora, `dnf`)        | Untested  | Command set present, flagged untested on a live host.                                                               |
| macOS (`brew`)               | Partial   | CPU/docker path (llama.cpp). No NVIDIA Container Toolkit on macOS, so the CUDA engines' docker path is unavailable. |
| Windows (WSL2)               | Untested  | WSL2 is detected and the dflash2 pin-memory rule fires; the command set is flagged untested.                        |
| Windows                      | Partial   | Code paths are only partially written; further development needed.                                                  |  

### Engines

| Engine            | Docker        | Local build        | State                                                                        |
|-------------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NInfer            | Yes           | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | The reference engine. Measured VRAM models for the Qwen 27B/35B artifacts.   |
| Hyper-Qwen (vLLM) | Yes (compose) | No                 | `.env`-driven docker-compose profiles.                                       |
| vLLM              | No            | No                 | Work-in-progress.                                                            |
| llama.cpp         | Yes           | Yes                | Specified, not verified until the binary is available.                       |
| Strata            | Yes           | No                 | Placeholder engine; its parameter surface is empty until the flag set lands. |

Runtime requirements: Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, pnpm 12.11.2 (pinned by `mise.toml`), and the `@deepseek-ai/cordis >= 4.0.1` peer dependency.

## Hardware guide

What each common machine gets you in practice. Capability impressions are sourced from [r/LocalLLaMA](https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/) user threads. "Shared" means unified memory (the model and the OS share the pool).

| Hardware                        | Memory          | What you get                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090                 | 32 GB VRAM      | Reliably fits model weights up to 23 GB with 240k+ context and vision. Handles complex coding and vision tasks, but needs special tooling for very long or complex tasks.     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The community workhorse. 30B-class models fit at Q4 and drive coding agents; 70B needs slow CPU offload. Best speed-per-dollar single card.                                   |
| NVIDIA RTX 3090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The used-card value king. Same 24 GB as a 4090 but an older generation: 32B at Q4 with modest context, no FP8. A single card is limiting; the common advice is to pair two.   |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000             | 96 GB VRAM      | Near-frontier dense models (70B–80B) fit fully in memory with long context, and 32B models can even be fine-tuned (LoRA, full FT). The prosumer ceiling.                      |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500             | 84 GB VRAM      | The rack-oriented 84 GB tier: 70B-class models with headroom, close to the PRO 6000 at a lower price point.                                                                   |
| NVIDIA Tesla V100               | 32 GB VRAM      | Cheap used HBM2 server card. 30B-class at Q4/Q8 at respectable speed (bandwidth is what matters for inference); no FP8, power-hungry. A budget homelab pick.                  |
| NVIDIA Tesla V100               | 16 GB VRAM      | The budget entry. 13B–14B at Q8, or 30B with offload. NVLink pairs double the capacity. Slow by modern standards, surprisingly solid for inference.                           |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 Laptop          | 24 GB VRAM      | The mobile 4090. 32B at Q4 just fits; realistically ~17B at Q4 once you subtract context.                                                                                     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 Laptop          | 16 GB VRAM      | The GPU is overkill for LLMs and the VRAM is underkill: 8B–14B at Q4/Q5 with small context.                                                                                   |
| NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)         | 128 GB shared   | The desktop AI dev box. A 35B

plugins.description: Scheduled idle-gated auto-update for DeepSeek Harness: DSH itself + installed plugins. Four schedule modes, bidirectional whitelist, web panel.
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-autoupdater **Auto-update plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** — 定时检查 DSH 本体与已安装插件的更新，只在无人使用的空闲窗口执行。四种调度模式、双向白名单、可视化设置面板。 English below · [English](#english) ## 功能 - **定时检查**：四种调度模式任选——每日 HH:MM / 每 N 小时（整点对齐）/ 每 N 天 / 每 N 分钟 - **空闲门槛**：会话日志 2 分钟无写入 + 无运行中 Agent 才动手；定时触发再叠加持续静默采样，绝不打断使用 - **插件批量更新**：遍历已安装插件，逐个对比 npm 最新版并升级（带 `包名@版本` 显式安装 + 磁盘回读验证，杜绝假更新） - **双向白名单**：白名单内只提醒 / 白名单内自动升级，两种语义随你切换 - **DSH 本体更新**：三种策略——不管 / 只暂存+通知 / 通知后宽限自动重启（宽限期内任何会话活动即推迟） - **Web 设置面板**：插件管理器内嵌卡片，改配置保存即生效（热配置，无需重启） - **最近活动日志**：每次检查/更新/重启都有可读记录，面板内直接查看 - **防变砖检查**：本体更新后校验 dsh 二进制存在才重启，npm 中断不留半更新状态 ## 安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-autoupdater ``` 或从 GitHub： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:/dsh-autoupdater ``` 安装后重启 DSH（systemd 环境：`sudo systemctl restart <你的dsh服务名>`），然后在 **插件管理器 → 自动更新** 卡片配置。 ## 配置 面板可改全部配置并即时生效；以下为 `cordis.patch.yml` 初始值： | 字段 | 默认值 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `scheduleMode` | `daily` | `daily` / `everyHours` / `everyDays` / `everyMinutes` | | `dailyTime` | `"04:30"` | 每日 / 每 N 天模式的锚定时刻 | | `everyHours` | `6` | 每 N 小时（整点对齐，1–168） | | `everyDays` | `1` | 每 N 天（锚定 dailyTime，1–365） | | `everyMinutes` | `60` | 每 N 分钟（1–10080） | | `idleSeconds` | `300` | 判定无人使用的持续静默秒数 | | `idleTimeoutMinutes` | `120` | 每次检查等待空闲的最长时间 | | `harnessMode` | `notify` | `off` / `notify`（暂存+通知）/ `auto`（宽限后自动重启） | | `graceMinutes` | `30` | auto 模式通知后的宽限分钟数 | | `systemdUnit` | `""` | 重启用的 systemd 服务名；空 = 从 cgroup 自动探测 | | `pluginMode` | `regexmode-ignore` | 白名单内只提醒其余自动 / 白名单内自动其余提醒 / 全自动 / 全提醒 / 关闭 | | `whitelist` | `[]` | 插件包名列表，含义随 pluginMode | ## 空闲判定原理 1. **会话日志 mtime**：`$DSH_HOME/sessions` 下任意文件 2 分钟内无写入 = 无进行中的工作（借鉴 [dsh-self-upgrade](https://github.com/raomaiping-hash/dsh-self-upgrade)，比 `agent.status` 可靠——实测 turn 结束后 status 可能停留 `running`） 2. **定时触发**额外要求持续静默 `idleSeconds` 秒，双重采样防瞬时空档误判 3. **手动触发**（面板"立即检查"）只要求此刻无运行中会话——你主动点的，不再等静默 4. 探测失败保守当忙，宁可不更新也不冒险 ## 本体更新的重启方式 - 配置了 `systemdUnit`（或自动探测到）→ `sudo -n systemctl restart `。**前置条件**：你的部署用户已配置该命令的 sudoers 免密，例如： ``` youruser ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart your-dsh-service ``` 未配置免密时 sudo 会失败，日志里如实记录，插件不会反复重试 - 未探测到 systemd → 按原 argv 脱离子进程拉起（兜底） - npm 全局安装后校验 dsh 二进制存在，缺失则**放弃重启**（防变砖） ## 安全模型 - 默认 `harnessMode: notify`——只暂存并通知，重启动作需你显式改为 auto - 空闲门槛不可绕过：面板不提供"忽略空闲"开关 - 更新前后均有磁盘版本校验，结果写入 `~/.dsh/autoupdater/history.jsonl` - API 仅写本地 `config.json`，不触碰系统配置 ## 已知限制 - 插件更新只覆盖声明 `dsh.bundle` 的 npm 形态插件；GitHub 源码安装的插件版本比对不适用 - 本体更新依赖 npm 全局安装形态（git checkout 形态请用 [dsh-updater](https://github.com/GodCC6/dsh-updater)） - 空闲判定基于本机 `$DSH_HOME/sessions` 的文件 mtime，远程会话（SSH 场景）不计入 ## 致谢 设计借鉴了社区同类项目：[dsh-self-upgrade](https://github.com/raomaiping-hash/dsh-self-upgrade)（会话日志 mtime 空闲判定、防变砖校验）、[dsh-updater](https://github.com/GodCC6/dsh-updater)（保守失败语义）、[dsh-auto-update](https://github.com/a1113622001/dsh-auto-update)（stage + 退出后应用架构）。 ## License MIT --- # dsh-autoupdater (English) **Auto-update plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** — scheduled update checks for DSH itself and installed plugins, applied only in idle windows. - **Four schedule modes**: daily HH:MM / every N hours (aligned to clock) / every N days / every N minutes - **Idle gating**: session-log mtime quiet for 2 minutes + no running agents; scheduled runs additionally require sustained quiet with double sampling - **Bulk plugin updates**: per-plugin npm version comparison with explicit `name@version` install and post-install disk verification (no phantom updates) - **Bidirectional whitelist**: whitelist-notified-others-auto, or the reverse - **Harness update strategies**: off / stage+notify (default) / notify then auto-restart after a grace period where any session activity defers it - **Web settings panel** embedded in the plugin manager; hot-reload config — changes apply without restart - **Activity log**: every check, update, and restart recorded and viewable in the panel - **Brick protection**: verifies the dsh binary exists after npm install before restarting Install: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-autoupdater`, then restart DSH and configure under **Plugin Manager → dsh-autoupdater**. See the Chinese sections above for full details — the configuration table and idle-detection notes apply to both languages.

plugins.description: Use the MiniMax Code (Mavis) subscription already signed in on this machine as a DeepSeek Harness model provider — with self-renewing credentials, a points/check-in panel and a model roster editor.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-minimax-connect

把本机 **MiniMax Code（Mavis）** 已登录的订阅接入 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)，作为一个模型 provider，并在设置侧边栏给出一个独立页面：**积分余额 / 每日签到 / 模型清单 / 用量**。

积分制账号：不消耗 API key，消耗 MiniMax Code 订阅的积分。

> **不用打开 MiniMax Code。** 插件自己完成 OAuth 续期，桌面客户端可以完全退出。
> 详见 [凭据自续期](#凭据自续期)。

English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)

---

## 为什么不需要"反代"

MiniMax Code 的推理端点**本身就是 Anthropic Messages 协议**，DSH 的 `pi-ai` 原生支持该协议。所以直接把请求打到官方端点即可，不需要中间代理进程，也不需要 hook 客户端。

`~/.minimax/config.yaml` 里 MiniMax 自己就写着：

```yaml
provider:
  minimax:
    npm: '@ai-sdk/anthropic'
    options:
      baseURL: https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1
```

## 实测契约（全部为真实响应，非推测）

| 用途 | 方法与路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 对话 | `POST {llm}/v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages 协议；流式返回 `thinking_delta` + `text_delta` |
| 模型清单 | — | `GET {llm}/v1/models` 返回 **503 `direct_route_not_configured`**；改从本地 `config.yaml` 静态解析 |
| 续期 | `POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token` | `grant_type=refresh_token`，见下 |
| 积分 | `GET {cloud}/credit/details` | `details[]` 带 `granted_amount` / `remaining_amount` / `consumed_amount` |
| 签到面板 | `GET {cloud}/signin/status?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai` | **`timezone_id` 是必需参数**，缺则 `1406010011 invalid timezone_id` |
| 签到 | `POST {cloud}/signin/claim?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai`，body `{}` | 空 body 与官方客户端一致；**同样需要 `timezone_id`** |

其中：

```
{llm}   = https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm
{cloud} = https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1
```

**注意两个 base 不同**：Anthropic SDK 会自己在 `baseURL` 后补 `/v1/messages`，所以 `{llm}` **不带**结尾的 `/v1`；而 cloud 路由**带** `/v1`。

## 鉴权

读 `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json`，取 `records[*].accessToken`（`mmoat_` 开头），以 **`Authorization: Bearer`** 发送。

> ⚠️ **不能用 Anthropic 的 `x-api-key`**：实测报 `401 {"code":401,"message":"token is required"}`。

记录键是 `` `${service}\0${account}` ``，分隔符是**真的 NUL 字符**，`account` = `base64url(sha256(authHome + "\0" + "mcode-public"))`。

## 凭据自续期

access token **有效期 1 小时**。MiniMax Code 大致每小时续期一次并写回同一个文件 —— 在它之外没有任何东西会做这件事，所以关掉桌面客户端后，插件在 token 过期的那一刻就废了：实测过期后第一个请求回 `401 invalid access token`，而记录里躺着一个完全可用的 `refreshToken` 无人问津。

本插件自己执行同一个 grant：

```
POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token
     grant_type=refresh_token
     refresh_token=<mmort_…>
     client_id=mcode-public
     scope=agent.default
     audience=agent-backend
  -> { access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in, scope }
```

行为：

- **提前 5 分钟续期**，不让任何一条流开在一个正在死掉的 token 上。除按需触发外，还有一条 60 秒的巡检。
- **`refresh_token` 单次有效、每次 grant 都轮换**，所以旧值在应答到达的瞬间就死了，新的一对必须在用新 access token 之前落盘。写入是**原子替换**（临时文件 + rename），桌面客户端不会读到写了一半的记录。
- **与官方客户端共存**。客户端用文件锁串行化自己的续期（`proper-lockfile`，`auth.lock` → `auth.lock.lock` 目录，`stale: 30_000`）。这里复用同一套 on-disk 约定：`mkdir` 抢占、超过 30 秒的锁按陈旧回收、写入前重新读一次文件并**采纳更新的 generation 而不是覆盖它**。两边轮流续期互不踢出，已实测双向共存。
- **两个文件必须同步推进**。客户端 `MCodeOAuthCore.readUsableCredential` 要求 `credential.generation === state.generation`，不一致就当成未登录。新代际取 `max(state.generation, credential.generation) + 1` —— 只用凭据自己的计数器，就可能写回一个**低于** `auth-state.json` 的值，把账号锁在自己的新 token 外面。
- **失败不抛异常**，一律回 `{ ok: false, reason, fatal? }`，调用方继续用盘上已有的 token。`fatal` 只标记一种永久失败：`invalid_grant`（refresh token 本身没了），此时只有去 MiniMax Code 重新登录一次能把 provider 救回来。

设一面卡片会直接显示当前状态：*自动续期已启用（到期前 5 分钟），不用打开 MiniMax Code* / *正在自动续期…* / *自动续期暂停，HH:MM:SS 后重试* / *凭据没有 refreshToken，需在 MiniMax Code 里重新登录一次*。

### 端到端验证

`test/renew-e2e.mjs` 只把 `expiresAtMs` 改到"即将过期"（**两个 token 一个都不碰**，所以 grant 失败也是零代价），然后调用插件自己发货的 `renewCredential`，最后拿新 token 打真实模型端点：

```bash
node test/renew-e2e.mjs ~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json
```

在 MiniMax Code **进程数为 0** 的情况下实测通过：grant 273 ms、代际 +1、两个文件代际相等、`loginEpoch` 保留、`refreshToken` 轮换，新 token 打 `/v1/messages` 返回 **HTTP 200** `{"text":"ok","base_resp":{"status_code":0}}`。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:VICqiufeeng/dsh-minimax-connect"
```

1. 装在 profile 的 `node_modules` 下，`dsh.profile.bundles` 会自动加上这一项。
2. **重启 DSH** 后生效。
3. 本插件不写用户补丁层（不碰 `cordis.patch.yml`），卸载时从 `dependencies` 与 `dsh.profile.bundles` 两处移除即可，不留残留。

如果 pnpm 的供应链闸门报 `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`（对 git 依赖一般不触发），追加 `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0`。

## 界面

**设置 → MiniMax**（`settings.section` 插槽，order 460），四个区块：

- **积分 + 签到 + 账号** —— 通用积分余额、七天签到面板、账号信息与续期状态。
- **模型清单** —— 逐模型开关 / 图片输入 / 上下文窗口（200K 或 1M）。
- **保存行** —— 落盘到插件自己的 settings 命名空间 `llm-minimax`。

同一份卡片也会出现在**插件管理页**（侧边栏「插件」图标 → 已安装 → `dsh-minimax-connect`）的详情里，因为它同时注册了 `plugins.bundle.config` 与 `plugins.row.config`。

另有一个自包含的零构建 HTML 面板：`GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel`。

## 路由（全部仅回环）

| 路由 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/status` | 汇总快照（面板用），含 `selfRenewal` |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/usage` | 积分明细原始应答 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/checkin` | 签到状态 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin` | 七天签到面板原始应答 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin/claim` | 执行签到 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/models` | 当前模型清单 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/__save` | 写回启用模型 / 图片开关 / 上下文窗口 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel` | 自包含 HTML 面板（无构建步骤） |

## 配置

`Config`（schemastery）可覆盖的字段：

| 字段 | 默认 |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm` |
| `cloudBaseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1` |
| `authFile` | `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json` |
| `configFile` | `~/.minimax/config.yaml` |
| `cacheMs` | `15000` |
| `enabledModelIds` / `imageOverrides` / `useMaximumContextWindow` | 由设置页写入 |
| 各 `*Route` | 见上表 |

## 模型

清单来自本地 `~/.minimax/config.yaml` 的 `whitelist` + `model_order`，默认四个：

| 模型 | 上下文 | 图片 | 推理 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MiniMax-M3` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 可开关 |
| `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |

## 已知限制

- **积分不换算成本**：模型描述符的 `cost` 全为 0。积分制下没有公开的每 token 单价，填 0 好过填一个编出来的数字。
- **依赖客户端非公开接口**：MiniMax 更新后端点可能变动；端点集中在 `lib/index.js` 顶部注释里，便于对照。
- **图片输入**走宿主的 durable attachment service。老版本宿主不提供该服务时会回 `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT`，插件对两种 store 形状都做了适配。
- 只测过 **Windows + 国内版（cn）**。区域路径与 `buildEnv` 硬编码在 `defaultAuthFile()` 里，其它区域需要改这一处。

## 设计说明

代码里凡是"为什么这么写"的地方都留了注释，几处值得一读的：

- `credential renewal` 段头：为什么插件不得不接管续期。
- `mirrorAuthState` / `nextGeneration`：两个文件代际必须一致的原因，以及那个会导致锁死自己的 off-by-one。
- `withAuthLock`：为什么复刻 `proper-lockfile` 的 on-disk 约定而不是依赖它。
- `adaptAttachmentStore`：宿主 attachment store 的两种形状。

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Adds sessions without a workspace to DeepSeek Harness
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session

为 DeepSeek Harness 增加**未分组（无工作区）会话**：点一下就开一个不占用任何项目工作区的会话，输入区仍是 DSH 原生那一个——模型选择、权限、附件、斜杠命令全部照旧。

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/yusunz/dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session)

## 为什么需要它

DSH 的输入区要求会话属于某个工作区；未分组会话在原生判定里是"空白会话"，输入区会被禁用。本插件在创建会话后，**临时**把它挂到与它自己工作目录同名的工作区上，让原生输入区可用；你发出第一条消息后，这个临时工作区被删除，会话落回**未分组**并照常保留、可恢复。

## 两个入口

| 位置 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| hero 行右侧 | 一枚「不在工作区中工作」按钮，与原生工作区选择框同一行；原生选择框保持原生，未被替换 |
| 右侧栏「开始」页 | 一张「非工作区会话」卡片，与「工作区文件 / 新建终端 / 浏览器」并列 |

两处动作一致：新建会话 → 临时挂载 → 原生输入区可用 → 首条消息后回到未分组。

## 工作目录

每次新建会话都会在工作目录下创建 `<YYYY-MM-DD>\<HH-MM-SS>` 子目录并作为该会话的 cwd，因此每个未分组任务互不干扰。

默认位置：`~/Documents/dsh`（可在设置里改）。

- **不留残留**：点了按钮却没发消息就切走，临时分组立刻消失；磁盘上那个空目录会在**下次启动 DSH 时**被回收。目录里只要有文件（代理写过东西）就永远不会被删。
- 会话本身从不被删除。

## 设置

**设置 → 通用设置 → 无项目任务文件夹**：显示当前路径，支持「更改」（宿主原生目录选择框）与「重置」（回落默认 `~/Documents/dsh`）。修改写入当前 profile 的配置并立即生效，之后新建的会话立即使用新位置。

## 安装

在应用内用插件管理器安装，或在命令行：

```bash
# npm
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session

# GitHub
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:yusunz/dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session

# 本地 tarball
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session-0.2.0.tgz
```

安装后**重启 DSH**（宿主半代码只在进程启动时加载），随后**硬刷新页面**（Ctrl+Shift+R）以确保取到新的客户端 bundle。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session
```

然后在应用内用插件管理器移除 bundle 并刷新页面。已创建的未分组会话不会被删除。

## 已知限制

- **右侧栏不能承载会话**：DSH 的右侧栏整套注册都绑定「当前会话」，标签页是文件 / 浏览器 / 终端这类面板类型，没有渲染对话面的座位。所以卡片点击后是在**主视图**打开会话，而不是在右栏开一个会话标签页。
- 放弃的空白会话回到未分组后遵循 DSH 原生规则：空白会话在侧栏不可见（有了消息才会作为普通会话显示）。
- 首条消息直接输入即可；附件走原生链路。

## 兼容性

- 目标：DSH 0.2.0 及以上的桌面版与 Web 版。
- 依赖：`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（DSH 自带，随插件声明）。
- 只在 `conversation.input.dock`、`conversation.hero.options`、`settings.general.item`、`sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` 这类**增量座位**上注册，不替换任何 DSH 原生控件。

## License

MIT

---

## English

Adds **sessions without a workspace** to DeepSeek Harness: one click opens a session that occupies no project workspace while keeping DSH's own composer (model, permissions, attachments, slash commands). The session is temporarily attached to a workspace named after its own directory so the native composer unlocks; after your first message that temporary workspace is removed and the session lands under **Ungrouped**, resumable as usual. Entry points: a button on the hero row and a card on the right sidebar's start page. Each session gets its own `<date>\<time>` working directory; empty ones are reclaimed on the next DSH start, and a directory holding files is never touched. Install with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-noworkspace-session`, then restart DSH and hard-refresh the page. MIT.

plugins.description: Read-only attachment library for DeepSeek Harness: every stored image and file, its size, and which conversations still use it.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-attachment-library · Attachment library

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds **Settings → Attachment library**: every image and file attachment stored on this machine, the space it takes, and which conversations still use it (active, archived, moving to the trash, or in the trash).

**Read-only.** Nothing is deleted: the plugin never creates, changes, moves, or deletes an attachment, a session log, a trash file, or a cache entry; "Show in Finder" only selects a file and never opens or runs it. The plugin's only write is the read-only copy "Open in Preview" places in the system temporary directory (outside DSH data), removed when the plugin stops. Its purpose is to check the reference counts before any cleanup is considered.

- DSH 0.2.x (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`, including the 0.2.1 alpha previews)
- Trash statistics work with [`dsh-plugin-session-trash`](https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-session-trash); without it only existing conversations are counted

## Install

**Desktop**: open **Plugins** in the sidebar → **Add plugin**, enter one of the following, click **Install**, then **Enable now** (new plugins start disabled):

- GitHub: `https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library`, or a version such as `github:ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library#v0.4.1`
- npm: `dsh-plugin-attachment-library`
- An absolute path to a local package, for example `/path/to/dsh-plugin-attachment-library-0.4.1.tgz` (made with `pnpm pack`)

Do not enter the source directory: its `node_modules` holds development copies of DSH packages that conflict with DSH's own.

**Command line** (optional): quit DSH, then run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-attachment-library`.

**Uninstall**: uninstall "Attachment library" on the **Plugins** page. The plugin stores no data; attachments are not affected.

## What the page shows

- **Totals**: all attachments (count and size); images and files; used by existing conversations, used only by conversations in the trash, and not used by any conversation (count and size each); attachments referenced but missing from the store; the size of the regenerable resize cache.
- **List**: a type icon (an image icon for images, an icon by extension for files), type, file names (every name stored for the same content), size, image dimensions and format, store time, and each referencing conversation with its title and status. An attachment shared by several conversations lists all of them.
- **Open in Preview** (macOS only): an arrow icon button on stored image rows (tooltip "Open in Preview") opens the image in Preview on the Host. Preview gets a read-only copy with the right extension, not DSH's own file (see below). File rows have no such button.
- **Show in Finder**: a folder icon button at the right of each stored row (tooltip "Show in Finder") selects the file in the Host's Finder (Windows Explorer, or the default Linux file manager): a file attachment shows under its real file name, an image as its content-named object file. It appears only when the page talks to the local DSH, the Host has a desktop file manager, and DSH allows desktop handoff; a failure is shown under the row.
- **Rescan**: the refresh icon button at the top right (tooltip "Rescan"); it is disabled while a scan runs, and "Rescanning…" is shown.
- **Filters**: type (all / images / files) and references (all / existing / trash only / unused); **sort** by time or by size (newest or largest first). The list shows 100 rows at a time.
- **Incomplete logs**: session logs that could not be read in full (damaged, cut short) are listed with a note that the "unused" counts may be too high.

## Why Finder shows no preview for images

DSH stores each image under its SHA-256 digest (for example `attachments/v1/objects/3f/3f9a…`) with **no file extension**, read-only (0400). The content is an ordinary normalized JPEG, WebP, PNG, or GIF, not encrypted; macOS decides the file type from the extension, so Finder shows no thumbnail and a double-click does not open it as an image. File attachments differ: each also has a read-only hard link under its real file name, which Finder shows normally.

## Counting rules

| Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Identity | DSH stores attachments once per content digest (SHA-256); images and files are stored separately, so the same bytes stored as an image and as a file are two rows |
| References | Every `{ type: 'image' \| 'file', attachment: { attachmentId } }` in a session log counts: user prompts, tool results, and system messages |
| Conversations | A subagent session's references count for the conversation that started it; a fork is its own conversation (it inherits its parent's prefix, so both are listed) |
| Existing conversations | Every session the session backend lists, read through the official read-only handle; status active, archived, or moving to the trash |
| Trash | Logs inside the trash directory are read directly (raw JSONL or Zstandard frames); the title is the one recorded when the conversation was moved |
| In use / trash only / unused | Any conversation outside the trash (including one waiting to move) makes it "in use"; only trashed conversations make it "trash only"; none makes it "unused" |
| Size | Each image object and file object counts once; file names are hard links and take no extra space; missing attachments add no size |
| Store time | The modification time of the stored object (when this content was first stored) |

## Cache

The first scan reads every session log and can be slow with many logs. After that:

- existing sessions are read again only when the session backend's revision changed;
- trashed sessions are read again only when the log file's device, inode, size, or modification time changed;
- image dimensions are cached by the same file facts.

The cache lives in the DSH process memory only and is never written to disk; the first scan after a DSH restart reads every log again.

## Configuration

Every DSH directory is only read.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `attachmentDirectory` | `<DSH home>/attachments/v1` | Attachment store; set it when `dsh-attachment-local` has its own `dshHome` |
| `trashDirectory` | `<DSH home>/session-trash` | Session trash; keep it equal to `dsh-plugin-session-trash`'s `trashDirectory` |
| `requestCacheDirectory` | `<DSH home>/cache/attachments/request-images` | Regenerable per-model resize cache; only its size is measured |
| `previewDirectory` | system temporary directory | Where the private temporary directory for "Open in Preview" copies is created; the only place the plugin writes |

## How "Show in Finder" works

- It uses DSH's own capability: the Host calls `revealNativePath` from the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command` (`open -R` on macOS, Explorer `/select` on Windows, the containing directory on Linux), the same function behind DSH's built-in reveal actions. Availability uses the same checks (`nativeFileManager()`, `canOpenNativePath()`); the browser also requires `ctx.remote.$host.isLoopback` and follows DSH's `session.canOpenWorkspacePath()` switch.
- The official `session.openWorkspacePath` is not reused directly: it takes an absolute path from the browser and only accepts paths mapped into the workspace filesystem, which the attachment store is not.
- The browser sends only the attachment kind and id (`sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits); the authenticated `/api` gateway validates them strictly and rejects any extra field, a path included.
- The Host derives the path from the id: a file is `attachments/v1/files/<prefix>/<digest>/<name>` (the first name in sorted order, or the `file-objects` object when none exists), an image `attachments/v1/objects/<prefix>/<sha256>`. The target must be a plain file inside the attachment store with no symbolic link on the way; anything else is "not found".

## How "Open in Preview" works

- The browser sends only the image id (`sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits); the gateway validates it strictly and rejects any extra field, a path included. The Host finds `attachments/v1/objects/<prefix>/<sha256>` and requires a plain file i

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-nonead-ursim

**A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that lets you control Universal Robots (UR) collaborative arms directly from natural language, developed by Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd. based on the same logic as the company's own nUR MCP Server.** ([Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd.](https://www.nonead.com))

This plugin shares the same ancestry as the company's `Nonead-Universal-Robots-MCP` (see "Reference implementation" below). It exposes the "control a UR robot with AI" capability as **native DSH tools**: the plugin starts a persistent Python worker (which internally reuses the vendored `URBasic` library), and tools talk to the robot through that worker. After a single `connect`, you can keep issuing commands to the same IP.

> 🧪 **Simulation-only by default (since 0.1.0).** This plugin drives **an offline, kinematics-level virtual UR robot** on the reserved loopback address `127.0.0.1` — and, unless you ask for more, nothing else. **In the default `motionMode: 'sim'` it has no real-robot channel at all**: a real IP is rejected as invalid input (`SIM_BADARG`) before anything is dispatched, and the vendored `URBasic` RTDE / Dashboard / SSH paths are unreachable from the tool surface. A real-robot channel **can** be enabled explicitly since 0.1.4 (`motionMode: 'real'` plus an allow-list — see *Real-robot channel (off by default)* below); the default above is unchanged by that. There is no `connect`-to-a-robot step: The simulation is started for you on demand (`UR12e`, upright pose, 100 % scaling), so the plugin works with **no real robot anywhere in the picture**. Commands that need a real controller (force mode, safety bits, programs, raw script, conveyor, power/brakes/freedrive) keep their tool names but answer honestly with `SIM_UNSUPPORTED` — they never fall through to a robot. Standard/tool I/O and the registers *do* have a simulation meaning since 0.1.5: an **in-memory state** where outputs can be written and read back, inputs have no producer (they stay at 0), and the registers have no writer (they stay at their initial values). **Telemetry is estimated since 0.1.6**: joint currents/voltages/speeds, TCP speed/force, the tool accelerometer and the joint temperatures come from finite differences plus an order-of-magnitude model, every reply carries `estimated: true` and a `note`, and the same values are added to `ursim_get_status` — which is what the simulation panel's telemetry row actually reads, so that row is no longer empty in simulation. The per-tool sections below are inherited from the real-robot code base and describe those semantics as they were; the behaviour that matters is the one stated here.

> ⚠️ **Safety notice**: this plugin's target is a simulation, so no physical motion can result from it. The safety warnings carried by individual tool descriptions apply to the real-robot code base this plugin was derived from.

> 🛡️ **Motion approval gate (opt-in; off by default)**: commands that physically move the arm, run a program, **take the arm out of program control, or remove its rigidity** — `ursim_movej` / `ursim_movel` / `ursim_movep` / `ursim_movec` / `ursim_run_sequence` / `ursim_servoj` / `ursim_move_optimized` / `ursim_move_x|y|z` / `ursim_move_tool_x|y|z` / `ur_draw_*` / `ursim_load_program` / `ursim_run_program` / `ursim_send_script` / `ursim_reset_error`; `ursim_set_freedrive` / `ursim_set_teach_mode` / `ursim_power_on` / `ursim_power_off` / `ursim_brake_release` / `ursim_unlock_protective_stop` / `ursim_shutdown` / `ursim_zero_ftsensor` / `ursim_set_conveyor_tracking`; `ursim_force_mode` / `ursim_end_force_mode` / `ursim_force_mode_settings` / `ursim_speedj` / `ursim_speedl` / `ursim_stopj` / `ursim_stopl` / `ursim_set_payload_inertia`, plus `ursim_motion_version`, `ursim_set_payload` and `ursim_set_gravity` — **need no human confirmation by default** (since 0.2.3 the product default is `requireApprovalForMotion: false`). The gate is a capability you can turn **on**: with `true`, those commands **pause and wait for human confirmation** before being sent to the robot, and a call made without an approval service, without an agent, or answered with anything other than `allowed-once` **fails closed** (the command is rejected and never dispatched). **Simulation targets** (`motionMode: 'sim'` plus the reserved loopback address) are exempt either way. The default lives in code (`config.requireApprovalForMotion ?? false`) and **matches** the schema default, so a caller that skips schema parsing behaves exactly like the product default; set `requireApprovalForMotion: true` to turn the gate on. `test/approval-gate.test.mjs` drives the real tool registry and proves all of the above, including that an extra `op` argument cannot re-route a call.

---

## Overview

`dsh-nonead-ursim` gives a DSH agent a **Universal Robots arm it can drive in plain language** — the
complete tool surface of a UR controller (87 `ursim_*` tools: joint and Cartesian motion,
multi-segment continuous sequences, OptiMove,
drawing primitives, pose and status readback, RTDE telemetry, standard/tool I/O and registers,
URScript, TCP/payload/tool settings, force mode, conveyor tracking), plus a live **3D simulation
panel** that renders the same joint data those tools read.

Out of the box it drives an **offline, kinematics-level virtual UR robot** on the reserved loopback
address `127.0.0.1`: no hardware, no real controller, nothing to install beyond Python — start a
simulation and issue commands. A real controller is addressed only after you ask for it explicitly
(`motionMode: 'real'` plus a `realRobotIps` allow-list), and the motion approval gate is **off by
default** (since 0.2.3; set `requireApprovalForMotion: true` to turn it on).

What the simulation models and what it does not is a deliberate, stated boundary: **motion is real
kinematics**; **telemetry is estimated** and labelled as such; **I/O and registers are in-memory
state**; anything that genuinely needs a controller (force mode, safety-status bits, program load and
execution, raw scripts, conveyor) answers `SIM_UNSUPPORTED` instead of pretending. It is **not** a
safety-assessment tool — there is no dynamics and no safety function — so cycle time, collision and
safety-distance questions stay outside its scope.

## Feature overview

**87** tools (`ursim_*`) in total.

| Category | Tool(s) (`ursim_*`) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | `ursim_connect` / `ursim_disconnect` | Connect / disconnect a UR robot by IP |
| Status | `ursim_get_status` | One-shot read of TCP, joints, model, serial, version, safety mode, run/program state, voltage, current, temperatures, uptime, joint currents/voltages/speeds, TCP speed and wrench, speed scaling |
| Pose | `ursim_get_tcp_pose` / `ursim_get_joint_pose` | Read current TCP pose / joint angles |
| Targets | `ursim_get_target_values` | Read **where the controller is *taking* the arm**: target joint positions/velocities/accelerations and target TCP pose/speed, plus the matching actual values for comparison. Comes from the RTDE `target_*` fields (added to the receive recipe in 0.6.0), so it is free — and it is the only direct evidence for "command sent but not executed yet / being blended / held back by the safety limit" |
| Device info | `ursim_get_robot_model` / `ursim_get_serial_number` / `ursim_get_uptime` / `ursim_get_software_version` / `ursim_get_safety_mode` / `ursim_get_safety_status` / `ursim_get_robot_mode` | Model (with `remote_control` field) / serial / uptime / software version / safety mode / **safety and robot status bits** (which safety function fired, incl. violation / fault; numeric limits must be read from PolyScope's Safety page) / run state |
| Programs | `ursim_get_program_state` / `ursim_load_program` / `ursim_run_program` / `ursim_stop_program` / `ursim_pause_program` / `ursim_list_programs` | Program state, load, run, stop, pause, SSH listing (`list_programs` works with the real robot's `/programs` and URSim `~/URSim_Linux-*/programs.*`; `load/run` accept full/URSim paths and `programs_dir`). **Run/stop/pause now check the controller's reply and report the run state**, instead of treating "could

plugins.description: Onto space panel for DeepSeek Harness: declarations, agents, memory and per-chat context.
plugins.readme_text:
# Onto Space Panel for DeepSeek Harness

A compact Onto space picker and a side panel for declarations, resident agents,
memory artifacts, templates and objects. Select what belongs in the current chat;
the active context remains visible above the composer.

## Features

- Connect to Onto on first use: enter your MCP endpoint and API key, verify
  access, then select a space. Reuse an existing Harness connection automatically.
- Search and select available Onto spaces.
- Open the space panel with **Обзор**.
- Read an accepted/current space declaration and attach it to the chat.
- Inspect resident agents and their charters. Selecting a valid active resident
  loads its accepted charter and constitution into the current chat.
- Search and page through accepted memory artifacts, read their contents and
  explicitly attach or disconnect them.
- Browse templates and objects, then include selected objects in the conversation.
- Keep selections and context separate for each chat and each selected realm.
- Change context through the `select_onto_space` and
  `configure_onto_chat_context` model tools when the user requests it.

The UI is currently in Russian. Names and descriptions are supplied by Onto.
An agent selection gives the current Harness conversation a resident role;
it does not launch a separate agent process or external agent broker.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with its Web UI or Desktop application.
- Your Onto MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, or an existing authenticated
  Harness MCP connection named **`onto`**.
- Harness's writable credential provider for the first-use setup form. Standard
  local profiles use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local`.
- The connection must expose `list_available_realms`, `about_realm`,
  `list_realm_agents`, `get_realm_agent`, `search_memory_artifacts`,
  `get_memory_artifact`, `get_memory_artifact_by_path`, `search_templates`,
  `search_objects` and `get_entity` for their respective panel features.

Host integration was developed against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2**.
Other releases are not yet verified. Harness is in developer preview and its
extension interfaces can change.

## Install a release tarball

Download the package `.tgz` from the project's release and install it into a
Web-capable profile. For example:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-onto-space-panel-1.2.1.tgz
```

Release downloads: https://github.com/hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel/releases

You can also install the tagged GitHub source, which already contains the built
browser entry point and has no install-time build script:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel#v1.2.1
```

In Desktop, use **Plugins** to install the downloaded bundle where supported by
your version. The tarball already contains the browser bundle; no install-time
build script or extra build permission is needed.

If this plugin was previously loaded manually by an absolute-path row in
`cordis.patch.yml`, disable that old row before enabling the packaged bundle.
Do not run two copies: they register the same tools and API routes.

Restart Harness after installing or replacing the bundle. Select an Onto space
above the composer and press **Обзор** to open its panel. Use **В контекст** to
attach a declaration or memory artifact. A role or material can be removed using
the `×` next to its context label.

## Connect Onto MCP

### First-use setup (recommended)

1. Install the plugin and restart Harness.
2. Click **Onto → Подключить** above the composer.
3. Enter your MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, then press **Подключить**.
   The key field expects only the value. A pasted `X-Onto-Api-Key: value` line
   is accepted too: the plugin removes the header name before sending or storing it.
4. The plugin checks access with `list_available_realms` before saving. After
   success, select a space from the list. An empty list means the connection
   works but no accessible spaces were returned.

Obtain the endpoint and key from your Onto administrator. The form uses HTTPS
and the `X-Onto-Api-Key` header; localhost HTTP is supported for development.
It requires a direct MCP endpoint, without credentials or query parameters in
the URL. Authentication redirects are rejected.

The connection belongs to the active Harness profile. Keys are stored through
Harness's credential provider, not in plugin configuration, browser storage or
chat messages. With the standard local provider, the managed credential file is
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`. This is local credential storage, not a claim of
OS keychain encryption. The server address and credential reference are stored
under `$DSH_HOME/storages/onto-connections/`, keyed by the profile location.
The plugin restores its own MCP connection on startup without editing profile YAML.

Open **Подключение** in the space picker, or **Подключение Onto** in the side
panel, to update a connection created by the plugin. A blank key reuses the saved
key only when the endpoint stays the same. Changing the endpoint or account key
requires choosing spaces and attaching context again; old chat context is not
automatically applied to the new connection.

If Harness already provides a server named `onto`, the plugin reuses it and
skips onboarding. Those external settings remain managed in Harness; the panel
does not overwrite or migrate that connection. A configured but unavailable
connection is shown as configured, with errors when loading spaces.

### Manual Harness configuration (fallback)

Use this when your deployment manages MCP centrally or does not provide a writable
credential provider. If the profile already has an Onto connection, do not add
a second one.

1. Obtain your Onto **MCP endpoint URL** and personal API key from your Onto
   administrator. Use the MCP endpoint, not the ordinary Onto website URL.
2. Open the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: normally
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` for Web or
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml` for Windows Desktop.
   A custom `DSH_HOME` changes the `.dsh` location.
3. Append the following patch, replacing the placeholder URL. If an Onto entry
   already exists, update it instead of creating a duplicate. The server name
   must be exactly `onto`.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-onto
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: onto
        transport: streamable-http
        url: https://YOUR-ONTO-MCP-HOST/mcp
        headers:
          X-Onto-Api-Key: !!js process.env.ONTO_API_KEY
```

This example uses Onto's `X-Onto-Api-Key` header. Confirm the authentication
scheme with your server administrator if your deployment differs.
A copy is available in [examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml](examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml).

4. Set `ONTO_API_KEY` in the environment of the process that starts Harness.
   For Web on Windows, start it from the same PowerShell window:

```powershell
$env:ONTO_API_KEY = 'YOUR_PERSONAL_API_KEY'
dsh --profile web
```

For Windows Desktop, fully quit Harness first, set the variable above, then
launch the executable from that same PowerShell window. For the default installer
location:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe"
```

Launching via an existing desktop shortcut does not inherit a variable set only
in this PowerShell window. The variable must be available on every launch.
Enter your real key locally; do not commit it or share terminal history containing it.

5. Open the space selector above the composer. Your accessible spaces should
   appear. You can also ask the model to call `mcp__onto__list_available_realms`.

If connection fails, check the endpoint and network access first. A `401` or
`403` response usually indicates authentication or access rights. If the tools
work in chat but the panel cannot find them, check that `serverName` is `onto`.
Missing agent or memory tools affect those sections separately; an empty list
can also mean your account has no access to those resources.

The transport and environment-variable syntax follow the official
[Harness MCP client configuration](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepse

plugins.description: DSHarness Go 互联插件，仅适配 DSHarness Go Android App。连接电脑工作区、会话、消息和任务。开源开发预览版。
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Go-workspace

**DSHarness Go 互联插件**。仅适配 **DSHarness Go APP**，将电脑上的 DeepSeek Harness 工作区、会话、消息和任务连接到手机。

[English](README.en.md) | [验证记录](docs/DSHarness-Go-M0.md) | [许可证及来源](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)

## 兼容性

当前是 M0 开发预览版 `0.6.4-desktop.9`。已在真实 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` 的独立 profile 验证安装和连接。旧版 DSH Desktop `0.1.5-rc.2` 尚未通过安装验收。

本项目的适配、支持和验收对象仅为 DSHarness Go APP。保留的上游网页能力和旧文档不构成对其他 App 或独立手机浏览器的适配承诺。

## 快速开始

1. 从 [当前 Release](https://github.com/Xiamen-Menggenda-Technology-Co-Ltd/DSH-Go-workspace/releases/tag/v0.6.4-desktop.9) 获取 `dsh-go-workspace-0.6.4-desktop.9.tgz`。这是预构建安装包，npm 尚未发布。
2. 在 DSH 的插件页使用本地安装包安装，启用 **DSH Go-workspace**，打开 **DSHarness Go 互联插件**。
3. 在电脑打开局域网连接和配对窗口，在 DSHarness Go 的“连接电脑”页面扫码或输入配对信息。

市场收录已提交 [PR #7579](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/7579)，尚待审核合并。目录使用上述 Release 安装包，市场收录后不依赖 npm 发布即可安装。按包名安装仍需等待 npm 发布，包名为 `dsh-go-workspace`。

DSH Web 可通过自己的 profile 安装实际下载的包：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-go-workspace-0.6.4-desktop.9.tgz
```

也可直接安装公开的预构建包：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/Xiamen-Menggenda-Technology-Co-Ltd/DSH-Go-workspace/releases/download/v0.6.4-desktop.9/dsh-go-workspace-0.6.4-desktop.9.tgz
```

`https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market` 是市场自身的源码仓库，不是本插件。市场自身安装报 `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` 时应使用已发布的 `dshmarket` npm 包；修复见 [市场 PR #890](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market/pull/890)。

Desktop 使用应用自身管理的 profile，上述命令不替代 Desktop 插件页安装。

## 能做什么

- HTTPS 配对、设备授权、撤销和连接管理。
- 为 DSHarness Go APP 提供工作区、会话历史、消息、任务和事件接口。
- 通过局域网或已有远程入口访问用户电脑。

## 连接教程

手机与电脑先处于同一局域网。电脑端生成短时配对信息，手机确认连接。保留原有设备记录、证书校验和授权机制。配对信息属于凭据，不要放到公开问题或截图中。

### 局域网访问

手机需能访问电脑所选网络地址；先在互联面板开启局域网访问，再打开配对窗口。使用可信网络时可参考[可信网络配置](docs/TRUSTED_NETWORKS.md)。

## 设备管理

在电脑端互联面板查看和撤销设备授权。改名保留 `mobile-access` 存储目录和 `dsh-mobile:` 配对协议，不要求清空用户数据。

## 安全

当前连接数据由用户电脑直接提供。本次没有部署账号服务器或中转服务。后续目标是服务器仅中转，消息和任务历史保存在用户手机；账号注册、登录同步、手机离线存储和端到端中转仍待实现。

[安全说明](SECURITY.md)。当前 DSHarness Go APK 只有调试构建，尚无经过正式签名验证的稳定版下载描述符。

## 扩展与自定义

保留上游扩展机制用于兼容现有配置；仅支持与 DSHarness Go APP 实际接口兼容的功能。

### 可选模块与高级配置

在互联面板管理客户端模块。模块开关和依赖限制见[客户端模块说明](docs/CLIENT_MODULES.md)；修改后按面板提示重新连接。

## 第三方插件适配

不承诺所有第三方插件组合可用。问题报告请包含 DSH、DSHarness Go APP 和本插件版本。

## 开发

```sh
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm pack
```

构建约束和实际验证范围见 [M0 记录](docs/DSHarness-Go-M0.md)。[贡献说明](CONTRIBUTING.md) 中的上游 Android 发布流程仅作历史参考。

## 致谢

感谢 [saya-ch/dsh-mobile](https://github.com/saya-ch/dsh-mobile) 项目及其维护者和社区贡献者，为本项目提供移动访问、设备配对和兼容性工作的基础。

DSH Go-workspace 在此基础上进行独立适配，专用于 DSHarness Go APP。详细来源和许可证见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

## 许可证

Apache-2.0 部分及 AGPL-3.0 部分分别保留许可。组合发行版包含 AGPL 代码，完整来源与许可见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)，不能将全部代码视为仅 Apache-2.0。

plugins.description: DSH plugin: wakes the agent when a long background task (download, install, wait) finishes after the turn has ended, so it reports back on its own.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-proactive · the night watchman

> A DSH plugin that lets the agent **speak up on its own** when a long job finishes
> after its turn has already ended — no more coming back to ask "is it done yet?".

[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-63%20passing-brightgreen)](#test-suite)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

[中文说明 →](README.zh-CN.md)

---

## What it does

You ask the agent to do something that takes hours — pull down a 40 GB model, wait for a
compile, sit through an installer. The agent starts the job, the turn ends, and it goes to
sleep. The job is still running. **Nothing tells the agent when it finishes**, so nothing
tells you either: you have to wander back and ask.

This plugin makes DSH watch the condition for you. When it is met, the plugin injects one
message into the session and wakes the agent — so the agent reports to you by itself.

```
you:      fetch that 20 GB thing and tell me when it's done
agent:    (starts the download → turn ends → asleep)
            ...hours later...
plugin:   *sees the file size stop changing* → *injects a message* → *wakes the agent*
agent:    "Done — 20.3 GB, and I verified the checksum against the published one."
```

## Why it exists

An agent is a request/response process. Once a turn is over it has no clock, no timer and no
way to learn that a `curl` it launched has exited or that a file has appeared on disk. Under
DSH the only thing that can hand it that fact is a message arriving in its inbox — which is
exactly what a session looks like when *you* type something. If nothing sends one, the agent
stays asleep until a human pokes it.

So the missing piece is not the waiting, it is the *waking*. This plugin is the thing that
wakes it.

## Mechanics

The wake-up uses the same call DSH itself uses when a subagent reports back to its parent
agent (see `dsh-subagent/lib/continuation.js`):

```js
agent.steer(createUserMessage({
    content: [{ type: 'text', text: message }],
    source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'dsh-proactive' },
}))
```

`agent.steer(...)` is the door into a session that is not currently running a turn;
`createUserMessage(...)` builds the message object that door expects. This is DSH's own API
surface, not a private back channel.

`source.kind = 'plugin'` is the default, and it matters: a plugin-originated message **is not
rendered in the UI**. You do not see a fake bubble pretending to be something you typed —
you only see the agent's reply, which is the whole point. `source.kind = 'user'` is available
per-entry if you deliberately want the message rendered as a user bubble, and it is used by
the test suite to prove the difference is real.

## Trigger types

| `type` | Fires when | Required fields |
|---|---|---|
| `file-stable` | The file size is unchanged across `rounds` consecutive checks — **the standard "download finished" test** | `path`, `rounds` (default `stableRounds`, 3) |
| `file-exists` | The path exists **as a file** (a directory does not count) | `path` |
| `file-size` | The file exists and its size is ≥ `bytes` | `path`, `bytes` (default 0) |
| `process-exit` | The named process is gone — **the job it was doing is over** | `process` (e.g. `curl.exe`) |
| `port-open` | A TCP connection to `host:port` succeeds — **the service came up** | `port`, `host` (default `127.0.0.1`) |
| `time` | The clock passes `at` — an alarm | `at` (ISO date-time; bare = local, `Z` = UTC) |

Unknown types never fire; they are skipped silently rather than guessed at.

### Common fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Identifies the entry in `boot.log` and in the default message. Any string. |
| `message` | What the agent reads when it wakes. Write it as an instruction to the agent, not as a note to yourself. |
| `sessionId` | Optional. Wake only this session. If it is not open, the entry is skipped for that tick and stays armed — it is **never** redirected to another session. Omit to wake the most recently active one. |
| `sourceKind` | Optional. `plugin` (default, not rendered) or `user` (rendered as a user bubble). |
| `form` | Optional, with `sourceKind: 'plugin'`. Free-form tag on the source; `notice` also carries a `summary` (first 120 chars of `message`). |
| `repeatSeconds` | Optional. Re-arm instead of firing once — see below. |

### Which session gets woken

When several DSH sessions are open, exactly one is chosen:

1. **`sessionId` set** → only that session. If it does not exist the entry is skipped, logged,
   and left armed. Refusing to fire is deliberate: a reminder delivered to the wrong session
   is worse than no reminder.
2. **`sessionId` absent** → the **most recently active** session. Activity means a message
   arrived in its inbox, its status turned `running`, or the session started. Not "the last
   one registered" — that older rule woke the wrong session when two were open, and it is
   pinned by five tests (`C. session selection`).

### One-shot versus repeating

A fired entry is stamped `fired: true` and never fires again. With `repeatSeconds` the entry
is **re-armed** instead, and `firedCount` / `lastFiredAt` record the history:

- `time` → `at` moves to now + `repeatSeconds`.
- `file-size` → `bytes` is raised to the current file size + 1, so the next byte appended
  fires it again.
- Any other type → `repeatSeconds` is meaningless and the entry silently degrades to one-shot.

Entries whose files are actually a moving target (a growing log, a progress file) are what
`repeatSeconds` is for.

## Install

One command, straight from the repository:

```bash
dsh plugin add --profile web github:mili1360/dsh-proactive
```

That resolves the package over git, adds it to the profile's `dependencies`, and registers
the bundle in `dsh.profile.bundles` on its own — verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`. Then **restart
DSH**: a registered bundle is only picked up at boot.

Works the same way from a local clone, if you would rather build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mili1360/dsh-proactive.git
dsh plugin add --profile web ./dsh-proactive
```

<details>
<summary>Doing it by hand instead</summary>

The plugin imports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, so it has to sit somewhere Node can resolve that
package from — a normal place for that is inside the profile's module tree.

```bash
# 1. put the plugin next to (or inside) your DSH profile
git clone https://github.com/mili1360/dsh-proactive.git ./dsh-proactive

# 2. register it in <profile>/package.json
#    dependencies:        "dsh-proactive": "link:<absolute path to the plugin>"
#    dsh.profile.bundles: [ "dsh-proactive" ]      <- add to the array
```

Then verify the import resolves from the plugin directory:

```bash
node -e "import('@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm').then(m => console.log('createUserMessage =', typeof m.createUserMessage))"
# createUserMessage = function
```

If that fails, link the package the way DSH exposes it — for example a `node_modules/@deepseek-ai`
junction inside the plugin directory pointing at `<profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai`.

**Restart DSH.** `dsh.marketplace.requiresRestart` is `true`, and a newly registered bundle is
not picked up without one. Afterwards the plugin directory contains `boot.log`, and three
lines mean it loaded:

```
apply() 被调用  enabled=true  intervalMs=15000
定时器已挂载
守夜人就绪
```

No `boot.log` means the bundle never loaded — check the profile registration again.

</details>

## Requirements / compatibility

**After installing, confirm it actually works — a profile that boots is not proof.**
A plugin can load cleanly, serve its routes and still break the host; we have seen exactly
that. So the acceptance test is: **create a new session and send it one message** (the plugin
is idle until a watch fires, so a quiet log is expected), then confirm the session exists and
the agent answered. If new sessions cannot be created at all, remove the mount line above and
restart.

Developed and tested against DSH **`0.1.0-rc.7`** — a **customised** build, not a stock
upstream release. Another version may register its services or name its events differently:
this plugin uses `ctx.on`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.agents`, the `agent/created`,
`agent/sessi

plugins.description: Pack de idioma espanol de Chile (es-CL) para la interfaz web de DeepSeek Harness: 2603 cadenas, plugin de cliente sin parchear la app.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-locale-es-cl

Pack de idioma **español de Chile (es-CL)** para la interfaz de **DeepSeek Harness** (DSH).

- **2.603 de 2.603 claves traducidas (100 %)**, repartidas en **57 namespaces**.
- **285 de esas 2.603 cadenas (10,9 %) se separan de la traducción castellana de partida**: es
  la adaptación chilena propiamente tal y está listada cadena por cadena, con su inglés y su
  referencia, en [docs/revision-es-cl.md](docs/revision-es-cl.md) y
  [docs/revision-es-cl.csv](docs/revision-es-cl.csv).
- Entra como **plugin de cliente** del Loader de DSH: **no parchea `app.asar`** ni ningún
  fichero de la aplicación.
- Cualquier clave que falte o que añada una versión nueva de DSH **cae automáticamente al
  inglés**, así que un catálogo incompleto degrada a la lengua de origen en lugar de
  romperse. El matiz importa: lo que cae a inglés es la **clave** ausente, porque el
  runtime resuelve con `?? key`; un namespace del que no se registrara **ningún**
  diccionario no tendría de dónde caer y mostraría sus claves en crudo. Eso último no
  ocurre en este pack —los 57 namespaces tienen diccionario—, pero es la frontera real
  de la garantía.

## Instalar en una línea

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:neobones/dsh-locale-es-cl
```

Recarga la interfaz (Ctrl+R) y elige **Ajustes → General → Idioma → Español (Chile)**. La
elección se guarda y sobrevive reinicios; un navegador en `es-CL` (o en `es`) lo activa solo.

Las demás vías —npm, tarball, instalación manual del perfil y qué hacer si el selector no
aparece— están en [Instalación](#instalación).

## Estado

| | |
|---|---|
| Cobertura | 2.603/2.603 claves (100 %), 57/57 namespaces |
| Adaptación chilena | 285/2.603 cadenas (10,9 %) distintas de la referencia castellana |
| Términos en inglés | 15 conservados por política, de los que **11 tienen claves que ejercerlos**; el informe de delta cierra con `protegidos 0` |
| Idioma | `es-CL` — etiqueta «Español (Chile)», respaldo `en` |
| Paquete | `dsh-locale-es-cl` 1.0.0 |
| Licencia | MIT (ver [LICENSE](LICENSE) y [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md)) |
| Núcleo de DSH probado | app de escritorio con `app.asar` de 121 MB, 70 plugins de UI |

La política de términos en inglés cubre **quince** palabras, pero el catálogo de la app solo
contiene texto para **once** de ellas: `plugin` (95 claves), `api` (25), `tool call` (23),
`token` (14), `json` (14), `prompt` (12), `log` (6), `shell` (5), `chat` (5), `diff` (4) y
`markdown` (4). Las otras cuatro —**`commit`, `push`, `pull request` y `deploy`**— no aparecen
ni una vez en el catálogo, así que se conservan como política declarada pero **no hay ninguna
clave que las ejerza**: `protegidos 0` mide las once primeras, no quince.

Estas comprobaciones se pueden repetir en cualquier momento y no necesitan la aplicación:

```powershell
node tools/build-locale-pack.cjs i18n/catalog.json i18n/es-cl . --check    # cobertura y marcadores
node tools/audit-es.cjs i18n/catalog.json i18n/es-cl                       # claves ausentes, desalineadas y repetidas
node tools/apply-terminology.cjs i18n/terminology.json i18n/es-cl --check  # términos y fraseología prohibidas
node tools/check-coherence.cjs i18n/es-cl                                  # concordancia y duplicados entre lotes
node tools/check-portable.cjs i18n                                         # ni rutas ni secretos locales
node tools/delta-report.cjs i18n/catalog.json i18n/reference/es.json i18n/es-cl --strict-protegidos  # protegidos 0 como puerta
node tools/verify-pack.cjs lib/client.js                                   # ejecuta el bundle como lo hace DSH
```

`delta-report.cjs` cierra `protegidos 0` y con `--strict-protegidos` **sale con código 1 si ese
total no es cero**: sin la bandera el total solo se informa (lo que necesitan los lotes
intermedios), con ella es una puerta. `check-coherence.cjs` tiene dos partes: la concordancia
junto a los términos en inglés y un barrido de duplicados que informa cuando un mismo origen
inglés produce más de una forma en español, o cuando dos orígenes distintos comparten una
misma frase hecha.

## Instalación

Basta una línea. El gestor de plugins que trae DSH añade la dependencia **y** selecciona el
bundle:

```powershell
# desde npm (lo más simple)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-locale-es-cl

# o directo desde GitHub, sin registro de por medio
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:neobones/dsh-locale-es-cl

# o desde un tarball ya empaquetado
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-locale-es-cl-1.0.0.tgz

# o el tarball publicado en la release (lo mismo, sin descargarlo a mano)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/neobones/dsh-locale-es-cl/releases/download/v1.0.0/dsh-locale-es-cl-1.0.0.tgz
```

Usa el perfil que realmente ejecutes: `desktop` para la app de escritorio, `web` para
`dsh web`. La instalación desde GitHub funciona **sin autorizar scripts de build**, porque el
bundle del navegador (`lib/client.js`) va versionado en el repositorio: no hay paso de
compilación que pnpm tenga que permitir.

El mismo resultado desde la interfaz: barra lateral → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, y pegas
la especificación. El gestor acepta nombre de paquete npm (con versión opcional),
`github:autor/repo` o una URL de repositorio git, un `.tgz` y una ruta local; comprueba que el
paquete declare `dsh.bundle` y al terminar lo añade a `dsh.profile.bundles`.

Después, **recarga la interfaz** (Ctrl+R) y elige el idioma en
**Ajustes → General → Idioma → Español (Chile)**. La elección se guarda y sobrevive
reinicios; un navegador en `es-CL` (o en `es`) lo activa solo.

### Vía manual: editar el perfil

Los plugins de un perfil se declaran en `~/.dsh/profiles/<perfil>/package.json`. Añade el pack
como dependencia **y** como bundle:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-locale-es-cl": "link:C:/ruta/a/dsh-locale-es-cl"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base",
        "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app",
        "dsh-locale-es-cl"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Después, en la carpeta del perfil:

```powershell
pnpm install
```

### Qué busca DSH para listar un plugin

Comprobado en el código de la aplicación (0.2.0-rc.2), por si hay que diagnosticar una tarjeta
que no aparece:

- `dsh.bundle.patch` en el `package.json` — **imprescindible**: sin ese campo el paquete se
  instala como dependencia plana, no como capa del perfil.
- La tarjeta se pinta con los metadatos que DSH lee de `locale/<idioma>.json`
  (`meta.title`, `meta.description`), con el `name` y la `description` del `package.json` como
  respaldo; el icono sale del campo `icon` de nivel superior. Para que el resolutor ESM los
  encuentre, el mapa `exports` tiene que declarar `./locale/*.json` y `./package.json`.
- `tools/check-plugin-meta.cjs` replica esas comprobaciones y corre en la integración continua.
- DSH **no** lee las palabras clave de npm ni consulta ningún catálogo propio: no hay nada que
  «indexar». El descubrimiento es el README, npm o el directorio de la comunidad.

### Notas

- La ruta `link:` y `github:` están soportadas por pnpm; la primera es la que está probada aquí.
- El fichero [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml) del paquete es lo que inserta la fila
  `locale-es-cl` en el árbol de plugins; lo aplica DSH al cargar el bundle, no hay que copiarlo
  a mano.
- Si tras instalar el pack no ves «Español (Chile)» en Ajustes, desactiva y vuelve a activar la
  fila `locale-es-cl` en el gestor de plugins para forzar una revisión nueva del bundle de
  cliente.
- **Aviso comprobado:** si modificas el perfil **desde dentro de una sesión de DSH**, la
  recarga en caliente dispone esa sesión y la aplicación abre una conversación nueva. Hazlo
  desde fuera o asume que esa conversación se corta (el historial no se pierde).
- El rescate «Disable third-party plugins» del escritorio deja el perfil con los bundles de
  fábrica, así que se lleva por delante este pack: para volver a tenerlo hay que reinstalarlo.

## Cómo funciona

Los plugins de cliente de DSH son fábricas *lazy-CJS* que el cargador ejecuta en el
navegador:

```js
window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory: (require) => { /* … */ return module.exports } })
```
